$\begin{aligned}P_{t r a p} & = & 5 x + \left(x - 3\right) + 5 x + \left(7 x - 3\right) \end{aligned}$

**Either expression formed **** [1]**

> *Form an equation by setting the expressions for the perimeter of the rectangle and the perimeter of the trapezium equal to each other.*

$\begin{aligned}4 x + \left(3 x + 4\right) + 4 x + \left(3 x + 4\right) & = & 5 x + \left(x - 3\right) + 5 x + \left(7 x - 3\right) \end{aligned}$

** **** [1]**

> *Simplify both sides by collecting the like terms together.*

$\begin{aligned}4 x + 3 x + 4 + 4 x + 3 x + 4 & = & 5 x + x - 3 + 5 x + 7 x - 3 \\ 4 x + 3 x + 4 x + 3 x + 4 + 4 & = & 5 x + x + 5 x + 7 x - 3 - 3 \\ 14 x + 8 & = & 18 x - 6\end{aligned}$

> *Solve the equation to find *$x$*, begin by subtracting the term with the smallest coefficient of *$x$*.*

$\begin{aligned}14 x + 8 & = & 18 x - 6 \\ - 14 x & = & - 14 x \\ 8 & = & 4 x - 6 \\ + 6 & = & + 6 \\ 14 & = & 4 x \\ \div 4 & = & \div 4 \\ \frac{14}{4} & = & x \end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Substitute *$x=3.5$* into the expression for the length and width of the rectangle.*

$w = 4 x = 4 ( 3.5 ) = 14$
$l = 3 x + 4 = 3 ( 3.5 ) + 4 = 14.5$

> *So  **w**  =  14 cm  and **l**  = 14.5 cm. *

> *Use this to find the area of the rectangle.*

$\begin{aligned}Area_{\left(r e c t a n g l e\right)} & = & 14 \times 14 . 5 = 203 cm^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$203\mathrm{cm}^{2}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Here is a rectangle and a right-angled triangle.

![q6-hard-2-13-forming-and-solving-equations-edexcel-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/2-equations-formulae-and-identities/forming-and-solving-equations/assets/017-q6-hard-2-13-forming-and-solving-equations-edexc.png)

All measurements are in centimetres.

The area of the rectangle is greater than the area of triangle.

Find the set of possible values of $x$.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Form an expression for the area of the rectangle.*

$\begin{aligned}A_{r e c t} & = & length \times width = \left(3 x - 2\right) \left(x - 1\right) \end{aligned}$

> *Form an expression for the area of the triangle using the formula *$A=\frac{1}{2}bh$*. *

$\begin{aligned}A_{t r i} & = & \frac{1}{2} \left(x\right) \left(2 x\right)\end{aligned}$

**Both expressions formed **** [1]**

> *Form an **inequality **by setting the expression for the area of the rectangle **greater than **the expression for the area of the triangle.*

$\begin{aligned}\left(3 x - 2\right) \left(x - 1\right) & > & \frac{1}{2} \left(x\right) \left(2 x\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Simplify the left-hand side by expanding the double brackets and collecting the like terms together.*

$\begin{aligned}3 x^{2} - 3 x - 2 x + 2 & > & \frac{1}{2} \left(x\right) \left(2 x\right) \\ 3 x^{2} - 5 x + 2 & > & \frac{1}{2} \left(x\right) \left(2 x\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Simplify the right-hand side by cancelling the 2s.*

$\begin{aligned}3 x^{2} - 5 x + 2 & > & \frac{1}{\cancel{2}} \left(x\right) \left(\cancel{2} x\right) \\ 3 x^{2} - 5 x + 2 & > & x^{2}\end{aligned}$

> *Rearrange to make this a quadratic equation equal to zero.*

$\begin{aligned}3 x^{2} - 5 x + 2 - x^{2} & > & 0 \\ 2 x^{2} - 5 x + 2 & > & 0\end{aligned}$

** **** [1]**

> *Begin to factorise by multiplying 2 by 2.*

*2 × 2 = 4*

> *Find two numbers that multiply to give 4 and add to give -5 (the middle number)*

*-1 and -4*

> *Split the middle term into -**x** and -4**x.*

$2x^{2}-x-4x+2>0$

> *Factorise fully the first pair of terms and the second pair of terms, either 2 or -2 could be factorised out of the last two terms, but the aim is to get the brackets the same so -2 should be factorised. *

$x \left(2 x - 1\right) - 2 \left(2 x - 1\right) > 0$

> *Factorise out the whole (2**x** - 1) bracket as if it were one term, leaving **x **and -2 in their own bracket.*

$\left(x - 2\right) \left(2 x - 1\right) > 0$

** **** [1]**

> *This means that the graph of *$y=2x^{2}-5x+2$* has roots at *$x=2$* and *$x=\frac{1}{2}$*.*

> *We are interested in the region where **y** is greater than 0, so this will be where the graph is above the **x-**axis. *

> *As the quadratic is positive, this will be in the regions above and below the roots.*

> * *$x>2\mathrm{and}x<\frac{1}{2}$

**allowing sign errors**** [1]**

> *Considering the expressions given for the length and width of the rectangle, we can find restrictions on the value of **x. **Remember that both the length and the width must be positive.*

$l = 3 x - 2 \Leftrightarrow x > \frac{ 2 }{3} ( \text{as} l > 0 )$
$w = x - 1 \Leftrightarrow x > 1 ( \text{as} w > 0 )$

> *As *$x>1$*, disregard *$x<\frac{1}{2}$*.*

$x>2$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
A cinema sells adult tickets and child tickets.

The total cost of 3 adult tickets and 1 child ticket is £30    
    The total cost of 1 adult ticket and  3 child tickets is £22

Work out the cost of an adult ticket and the cost of a child ticket.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Let adult tickets be **a** and child tickets be **c. *

> *Use the information in the question to write two equations.*

> *3 adult tickets = 3**a, **1 child ticket = **c,** add these and set equal to 30. *

$3a+c=30$

> *1 adult ticket = **a, **3 child tickets = 3**c,** add these and set equal to 22. *

$a+3c=22$

**[1]**

> *Number the equations.*

> $\begin{aligned}3 a + c & = & 30 \left(1\right) \\ a + 3 c & = & 22 \left(2\right)\end{aligned}$* *

> *Make the **c** terms equal by multiplying all parts of equation (1) by 3.*

> $3 ( 1 ) 3 ( 3 a + c = 30 )$
$( 2 ) a + 3 c = 22$*  *

> *This gives the two equation with the same coefficient of **c.*

$\begin{aligned}9 a + 3 c & = & 90 \left(3\right) \\ a + 3 c & = & 22 \left(2\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Eliminate the **c** terms by subtracting equation (2) from equation (3).*

$\begin{gathered} 9 \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} a \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} + \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} 3 \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} c \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} = \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} 90 \end{gathered}$
$\underline{-\ (a + 3c = 22)}$
$8a = 68$

**[1]**

> *Solve the equation to find** a  **by dividing both sides by 8.*

$\begin{aligned}a & = & \frac{68}{8} = 8 . 5\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute *$a=8.5$* into either of the two original equations**.*

$\begin{aligned}\left(1\right) 3 a + c & = & 30 \\ 3 \left(8 . 5\right) + c & = & 30 \\ 25 . 5 + c & = & 30\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Solve this equation to find** c.*

$\begin{aligned}c + 25 . 5 & = & 30 \\ c & = & 30 - 25 . 5 \\ c & = & 4 . 5 \end{aligned}$

> *This means that 1 adult ticket costs £8.50 and 1 child ticket costs £4.50. *

**Adult ticket = £8.50 **
**      Child ticket =  £4.50 ****[1]**

parts.problemMd:
3 teas and 2 coffees have a total cost of £7.80 
5 teas and 4 coffees have a total cost of £14.20

Work out the cost of one tea and the cost of one coffee.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Let the cost of a tea be **t** and the cost of a coffee be **c. *

> *Use the information in the question to write two equations.*

> *3 teas = 3**t, **2 coffees = 2**c,** add these and set equal to 7.8 (£7.80). *

$3t+2c=7.8$

> *5 teas = 5**t, **4 coffees = 4**c,** add these and set equal to 14.2 (£14.20). *

$5t+4c=14.2$

**[1]**

> *Number the equations.*

> $\begin{aligned}3 t + 2 c & = & 7 . 8 \left(1\right) \\ 5 t + 4 c & = & 14 . 2 \left(2\right)\end{aligned}$* *

> *Make the **c** terms equal by multiplying all parts of equation (1) by 2.*

$2 ( 1 ) 2 ( 3 t + 2 c = 7.8 )$
$( 2 ) \begin{array}{rcl} \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} 5 \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} t \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} + \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} 4 \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} c \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} = \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} 14 \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} . \end{array} \begin{array}{rcl} 2 \end{array}$*  *

> *This gives two equations with the same coefficient of **c.*

$\begin{aligned}6 t + 4 c & = & 15 . 6 \left(3\right) \\ 5 t + 4 c & = & 14 . 2 \left(2\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Eliminate the **c** terms by subtracting equation (2) from equation (3).*

$\begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} 6 \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} t \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} + \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} 4 \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} c \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} = \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} 15 \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} . \end{gathered} \begin{gathered} 6 \end{gathered}$
$\underline{-\ (5t + 4c = 14.2)}$
$t = 1.4$

**[1]**

> *Substitute *$t=1.4$* into either of the two original equations**.*

$\begin{aligned}\left(1\right) 3 t + 2 c & = & 7 . 8 \\ 3 \left(1 . 4\right) + 2 c & = & 7 . 8 \\ 4 . 2 + 2 c & = & 7 . 8\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Solve this equation to find** c.*

$\begin{aligned}2 c & = & 7 . 8 - 4 . 2 \\ 2 c & = & 3 . 6 \\ c & = & \frac{3 . 6}{2} = 1 . 8\end{aligned}$

> *This means that 1 tea costs £1.40 and 1 coffee costs £1.80. *

**One tea = £1.40    **
**   One coffee = £1.80 ****[1]**

The diagram shows a trapezium.

All the measurements are in centimetres.

The area of the trapezium is 351 cm<sup>2</sup>.

Show that  $2x^{2}+x---351=0$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Substitute the values in the diagram into the formula for the area of a trapezium. *

> *The formula is *$A = \frac{1}{2} \left(a + b\right) h$*, where *$a$* and *$b$* are the two parallel sides and *$h$* is the perpendicular height.*

$A = \frac{1}{2} \times \left(\left(x - 4\right) + \left(x + 5\right)\right) \times 2 x$

**[1]**

> *The area is given as 351 cm*<sup>*2*</sup>*, so set this expression equal to 351.*

$\frac{1}{2} \times \left(\left(x - 4\right) + \left(x + 5\right)\right) \times 2 x = 351$

> *Simplify the expression in the brackets.*

$\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{2} \times \left(2 x + 1\right) \times 2 x & = & 351\end{aligned}$

> *Cancel out the 2.*

$\begin{aligned} \frac{1}{\cancel{2}} \times \left(2 x + 1\right) \times \cancel{2} x & = & 351 \\ x \left(2 x + 1\right) & = & 351\end{aligned}$

> *Expand the brackets on the right hand side.*

$\begin{aligned}2 x^{2} + x & = & 351\end{aligned}$

> *Subtract 351 from both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}2 x^{2} + x - 351 & = & 0\end{aligned}$

$2x^{2}+x-351=0$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Work out the value of $x$.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Substitute the given values into the quadratic formula*

> *Given an equation of the form *$ax^{2}+bx+c=0$*, the quadratic formula is *$x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}$*.*

> *Identify the values of **a, b **and **c.*

$a=2,b=1,c=-351$

> *Substitute into the quadratic formula.*

$x=\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{1^{2}-4\times2\times-351}}{2\times2}$

** [1]**

> *Simplify the right hand side.*

$x=\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{2809}}{4}$

** [1]**

> *Work out the two results by doing the calculation twice, once using the positive sign and once using the negative sign in front of the square root.*

$x=13$* or *$x=-13.5$

> *Considering the diagram in part (a), the height of the trapezium is *$2x$*, so *$x$* must be positive.*

** **$x=13$** ****[1]**

parts.solutionMd:

> *Rectangle **A** has a length of 15 m and a width of 8 m.*

$\mathrm{Area}_{A}=15\times8=120$

> *Rectangle **B** has a length of *$\left(15 - x\right)$* m and a width of 3 m.*

$Area_{B} = 3 \left(15 - x\right)$

**[1]**

> *Write down an expression for the total area of the floor plan by adding the two expressions together.*

$Area = 120 + 3 \left(15 - x\right)$

> *Write an **equation **for the area by setting the expression for the area equal to 138.*

**[1]**

parts.problemMd:
In a chess club, there are $x$ boys and $y$ girls.

If 5 more boys and 8 more girls join, there would be half as many boys as girls.

Show that $y=2x+2$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Method 1*

> *If 5 more boys and 8 more girls join there will be *

$x+5$* **boys and *$y+8$* girls*

> *If there are half as many boys as girls then;*

$x + 5 = \frac{1}{2} \left(y + 8\right)$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 2 to clear the fraction.*

$2x+10=y+8$

> *And subtract 8 from both sides.*

$2x+2=y$** [1]**

> *Method 2*

> *If 5 more boys and 8 more girls join there will be *

$x+5$* **boys and *$y+8$* girls*

> *If there are half as many boys as girls then;*

$2 \left(x + 5\right) = y + 8$

**[1]**

> *Expand the bracket.*

$2x+10=y+8$

> *And subtract 8 from both sides.*

$2x+2=y$** [1]**

parts.problemMd:
If instead,

10 more boys and 1 more girl join, there would be the same number of boys and girls.

Work out $x$ and $y$.

$x$ = ...................

$y$ = ...................
parts.solutionMd:
> *If 10 more boys and 1 more girls join there will be;*

*'*$x+10$*' boys and '*$y+1$*' girls*

> *The number of boys equals the number of girls.*

$x+10=y+1$

**[1]**

> *Subtract one from both sides.*

$x+9=y$

> *If we combine this with the equation given in part (a), then we have a pair of simultaneous equations.*

$y=x+9\mathrm{and}y=2x+2$

> *We can solve these by elimination or substitution. Here we will use substitution.*

$x+9=2x+2$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}x + 9 & = & 2 x + 2 \\ - x & = & - x \\ 9 & = & x + 2 \\ - 2 & = & - 2 \\ 7 & = & x\end{aligned}$

> *Solve, in this case by subtracting  *$\begin{aligned} & & x\end{aligned}$* and then subtracting 2 from both sides.*

$x=7$** [1]**

> *Be careful! We have not fully answered the question until we have found *$\begin{aligned} & & y\end{aligned}$*. Substitute *$\begin{aligned}x & = & 7\end{aligned}$* into *$\begin{aligned}y & = & x + 9\end{aligned}$* or *$\begin{aligned}y & = & 2 x + 2\end{aligned}$*.*

$\begin{aligned}y & = & 7 + 9 = 16 or y = 2 \left(7\right) + 2 = 16\end{aligned}$

$y=16$* ***[1]**

**Perform a mental check; "7 boys and 10 more join means 17 boys; 16 girls and one more joins means 17 girls; the same number of boys and girls" **

parts.problemMd:
Theo starts with savings of £18

James starts with no savings.

Each week from now,

Theo will save £4.50 and James will save £4

In how many weeks will Theo and James have savings in the ratio 15 : 8 ?
parts.solutionMd:
> *You could do this by trial and error, adding £4.50 and £4 to their respective totals over and over and checking each time whether the ratio has become 15 : 8. *

> *That could take a long time, however, so it's better to use a more algebraic approach.*

> *Call the number of weeks from the start "**N **". Then write a formula in terms of **N** for how much they each have after **N** weeks.*

$\mathrm{Theo}:18+4.5N\,\,\mathrm{James}:4N$

Rana sells 192 cakes in the ratio    small : medium : large    =    7 : 6 : 11

The profit for one medium cake is twice the profit for one small cake. 
The profit for one large cake is three times the profit for one small cake.

parts.solutionMd:
> *Start by working out how many of each size cake she makes. Add up the ratio numbers to find the number of 'parts' that the 192 cakes are divided into.*

> * Then divide 192 by that sum to find the size of one part.*

$7+6+11=24\,\,192\div24=8$

**[1]**

> *So one part is 8 cakes. *

> *To find the amount of each size of cake, multiply 8 by the respective ratio numbers.*

$\mathrm{small}:8\times7=56\,\,\mathrm{medium}:8\times6=48\,\,\mathrm{large}:8\times11=88$

> *Then the profit for a medium cake is 2**x**, and the profit for a large cake is 3**x. *

> *Use this and the numbers of cakes from above to set up an equation equal to the total profit. *

> *Begin to solve the equation.*

$( 56 \times x ) + ( 48 \times 2 x ) + ( 88 \times 3 x ) = 532.48$

56 x space plus space 96 x space plus 264 x space equals space 532.48

416 x space equals space 532.48

**[1] **
**The mark here is for setting up a correct equation.**

> *Finish solving the equation to find the value of **x**  (which is also the profit for one small cake).*

$x=532.48\div416=1.28$

**[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Here are two right-angled triangles.

![q2-veryhard-2-13-forming-and-solving-equations-edexcel-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/2-equations-formulae-and-identities/forming-and-solving-equations/assets/008-q2-veryhard-2-13-forming-and-solving-equations-e.png)

Given that

$\mathrm{tan}e=\mathrm{tan}f$

find the value of $x$.

You must show all your working.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Both triangles are right-angled triangles so use SOHCAHTOA. You know the length of the opposite (**O**) and the length of the side adjacent (**A**) to the angle. *

> *Therefore the tangent ratio can be used to write expressions for the tangent ratio for both triangles, *$\mathrm{tan}θ=\frac{O}{A}$*.*

$\mathrm{tan}e=\frac{x}{4x-1}$

$\mathrm{tan}f=\frac{6x+5}{12x+31}$

> *Use the given information, *$\mathrm{tan}e=\mathrm{tan}f$*, to write an equation in terms of *$x$*.*

$\begin{aligned}tan e & = & tan f \\ \frac{x}{4 x - 1} & = & \frac{6 x + 5}{12 x + 31}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Remove the fraction on the LHS by multiplying both sides by *$\left(4 x - 1\right)$*.*

$\begin{aligned}\left(4 x - 1\right) \frac{x}{4 x - 1} & = & \frac{6 x + 5}{12 x + 31} \left(4 x - 1\right) \\ x & = & \frac{\left(6 x + 5\right) \left(4 x - 1\right)}{12 x + 31}\end{aligned}$

> *Remove the fraction on the RHS by multiplying both sides by *$\left(12 x + 31\right)$*.*

$\begin{aligned}x \left(12 x + 31\right) & = & \frac{\left(6 x + 5\right) \left(4 x - 1\right)}{12 x + 31} \left(12 x + 31\right) \\ x \left(12 x + 31\right) & = & \left(6 x + 5\right) \left(4 x - 1\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Expand the brackets on both sides of the equation.*

$\begin{aligned}x \left(12 x + 31\right) & = & \left(6 x + 5\right) \left(4 x - 1\right) \\ 12 x^{2} + 31 x & = & 24 x^{2} - 6 x + 20 x - 5 \\ 12 x^{2} + 31 x & = & 24 x^{2} + 14 x - 5\end{aligned}$

> *Rearrange the expression to make a quadratic equation equal to 0.*

$\begin{aligned}0 & = & 24 x^{2} + 14 x - 5 - \left(12 x^{2} + 31 x\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Simplify.*

$\begin{aligned}24 x^{2} + 14 x - 5 - 12 x^{2} - 31 x & = & 0 \\ 12 x^{2} - 17 x - 5 & = & 0\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *This could be solved by factorising or using the quadratic formula, the formula may be easier.*

> *Substitute the given values into the quadratic formula*

> *Given an equation of the form *$ax^{2}+bx+c=0$*, the quadratic formula is *$x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}$*.*

> *Identify the values of **a, b **and **c.*

$a=12,b=-17,c=-5$

> *Substitute into the quadratic formula.*

$x = \frac{- \left(- 17\right) \pm \sqrt{\left(- 17\right)^{2} - 4 \times 12 \times \left(- 5\right)}}{2 \times 12}$

** [1]**

> *Simplify.*

$x=\frac{17\pm\sqrt{529}}{24}$

> *Work out the two results by doing the calculation twice, once using the positive sign and once using the negative sign in front of the square root.*

$x=\frac{5}{3}$* ** or  *$x=-\frac{1}{4}$

> *Considering the diagram in part (a), the height of the first triangle is *$x$*, so *$x$* must be positive.*

** **$x=\frac{5}{3}$** ****[1]**

parts.problemMd:
![q3-veryhard-2-13-forming-and-solving-equations-edexcel-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/2-equations-formulae-and-identities/forming-and-solving-equations/assets/007-q3-veryhard-2-13-forming-and-solving-equations-e.png)

The lengths of the sides are in centimetres.

The area of triangle $T_{1}$ is equal to the area of triangle $T_{2}$. 
Work out the value of $x$, giving your answer in the form $a+\sqrt{b}$ where $a$ and $b$ are integers.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Form an expression for the area of triangle *$T_{1}$* using the formula for the area of a triangle if the perpendicular height is **not **known. *

> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$A=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where *$a$* and *$b$* are the two known sides and *$C$* is the included angle.*

$Area_{T_{1}} = \frac{1}{2} \left(x\right) \left(x\right) sin \left(30 \circ\right)$

**[1]**

> *Form an expression for the area of triangle *$T_{2}$* using the formula for the area of a triangle if the perpendicular height **is **known. The formula for the area of a triangle is *$A=\frac{1}{2}bh$*, where *$b$* is the base and *$h$* is the height perpendicular to the base.*

$Area_{T_{2}} = \frac{1}{2} \left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)$

**[1]**

> *Use the given information, *$\mathrm{area}T_{1}=\mathrm{area}T_{2}$*, to write an equation in terms of *$x$*.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} \left(x\right) \left(x\right) sin \left(30 \circ\right) & = & \frac{1}{2} \left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Cancel *$\frac{1}{2}$*, which exists on both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}\left(x\right) \left(x\right) sin \left(30 \circ\right) & = & \left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right) \\ x^{2} sin 30 & = & \left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Use your knowledge of trig exact values, or your calculator, to evaluate *$sin 30 \circ \left(= \frac{1}{2}\right)$*.*

$\begin{aligned}x^{2} \left(\frac{1}{2}\right) & = & \left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right) \\ \frac{1}{2} x^{2 } & = & \left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Expand the brackets on the RHS of the equation.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} x^{2 } & = & \left(x - 2\right) \left(x + 1\right) \\ \frac{1}{2} x^{2 } & = & x^{2} + x - 2 x - 2 \\ \frac{1}{2} x^{2 } & = & x^{2} - x - 2\end{aligned}$

> *REmove the fraction by multiplying both sides by 2.*

$\begin{aligned}x^{2 } & = & 2 \left(x^{2} - x - 2\right) \\ & = & 2 x^{2} - 2 x - 4\end{aligned}$

> *Rearrange the expression to make a quadratic equation equal to 0.*

$\begin{aligned}0 & = & 2 x^{2} - 2 x - 4 - x^{2}\end{aligned}$

> *Simplify.*

$\begin{aligned}2 x^{2} - 2 x - 4 - x^{2} & = & 0 \\ x^{2} - 2 x - 4 & = & 0\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *The question asks for the answer to be given in the form *$a+\sqrt{b}$*, where *$a$* and *$b$* are integers. *

> *This form can be obtained by either using the quadratic formula, or by completing the square.*

> *Given an equation of the form *$ax^{2}+bx+c=0$*, the quadratic formula is *$x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}$*.*

> *Identify the values of **a, b **and **c.*

$a=1,b=-2,c=-4$

> *Substitute into the quadratic formula.*

$x = \frac{- \left(- 2\right) \pm \sqrt{\left(- 2\right)^{2} - 4 \times 1 \times \left(- 4\right)}}{2 \times 1}$

> *Simplify.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{20}}{2} \\ & = & \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 \times 5}}{2} \\ & = & \frac{2 \pm \sqrt{4} \sqrt{5}}{2} \\ & = & \frac{2 \pm 2 \sqrt{5}}{2}\end{aligned}$

> *Cancel out 2 from each term.*

$x = \begin{aligned} & & \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & 1\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & +\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}$* **  or  *$x = \begin{aligned} & & \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & 1\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & -\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}$

> *Considering the diagram in part (a), the lengths of *$T_{1}$* are *$x$*, so *$x$* must be positive. The value *$1-\sqrt{5}$* is negative so this cannot be the length of a triangle. *

** **$x=1+\sqrt{5}$** ****[1]**

parts.problemMd:
There are only $r$ red counters and $g$ green counters in a bag.

A counter is taken at random from the bag.

The probability that the counter is green is $\frac{3}{7}$

The counter is put back in the bag.

2 more red counters and 3 more green counters are put in the bag. 
A counter is taken at random from the bag.

The probability that the counter is green is $\frac{6}{13}$

Find the number of red counters and the number of green counters that were in the bag originally.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Identify the number of each counters*

| > *Red* | > *Green* | > *Total* |
|---|---|---|
| $r$ | $g$ | $r+g$ |

> *Use the probability  *$\frac{3}{7}$* to form an equation*

$\frac{g}{r+g}=\frac{3}{7}$

**[1]**

> *Identify the number of each counters*

| > *Red* | > *Green* | > *Total* |
|---|---|---|
| $r+2$ | $g+3$ | $r+g+5$ |

> *Use the probability  *$\frac{6}{13}$* to form an equation*

$\frac{g+3}{r+g+5}=\frac{6}{13}$

**[1]**

> *Rewrite both equations without the fractions*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{g}{r + g} & = & \frac{3}{7} \\ 7 g & = & 3 \left(r + g\right) \\ 7 g & = & 3 r + 3 g \\ 4 g & = & 3 r\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\frac{g + 3}{r + g + 5} & = & \frac{6}{13} \\ 13 \left(g + 3\right) & = & 6 \left(r + g + 5\right) \\ 13 g + 39 & = & 6 r + 6 g + 30 \\ 7 g + 9 & = & 6 r\end{aligned}$

**writing both without fractions [1]**

> *Double the first equation*

$\begin{aligned}6 r & = & 8 g\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute into the second equation*

$\begin{aligned}8 g & = & 7 g + 9 \\ g & = & 9\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Substitute *$g=9$* into the first equation to find *$r$

$\begin{aligned}3 r & = & 4 \times 9 \\ 3 r & = & 36 \\ r & = & 12\end{aligned}$

**9 green and 12 red ****[1]**

parts.solutionMd:
> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$A=\frac{1}{2}bh$*, where *$b$* is the base and *$h$* is the height perpendicular to the base.*

> *Remove the fraction by multiplying both sides by 2.*

> *Expand the brackets on the LHS of the equation.*

**[1]**

> *This cannot be factorised, so solve to find *$x$* by either using the quadratic formula, or by completing the square.*

> *Given an equation of the form *$ax^{2}+bx+c=0$*, the quadratic formula is *$x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}$*.*

> *Identify the values of **a, b **and **c.*

> *Substitute into the quadratic formula.*

> *Simplify.*

parts.problemMd:
The total surface area of a solid hemisphere is equal to the curved surface area of a cylinder.

The radius of the hemisphere is $r$ cm.

The radius of the cylinder is twice the radius of the hemisphere.

Given that

$\mathrm{volume} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{hemisphere}:\mathrm{volume} \mathrm{of} \mathrm{cylinder}=1:m$

find the value of $m$.
parts.solutionMd:
> *The total surface area of a hemisphere is*

$\begin{aligned}S A_{h e m i s p h e r e} & = & \frac{1}{2} \times 4 \pi r^{2} + \pi r^{2} \\ & = & 3 \pi r^{2}\end{aligned}$

> *Now that we have used *$r$* as the radius of the hemisphere, let *$R$* be the radius of the cylinder (and let its height be *$h$*). The curved surface area of the cylinder is therefore*

$SA_{cylinder}=2πRh$

> *"The radius of the cylinder is twice the radius of the hemisphere" therefore*

$R=2r$

> *Substitute this into the formula for the curved surface area of the cylinder*

$\begin{aligned}S A_{c y l i n d e r} & = & 2 \pi \left(2 r\right) h \\ & = & 4 \pi r h\end{aligned}$

> *Equate the formulae for the surface areas of the hemisphere and the cylinder*

$3πr^{2}=4πrh$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange to get *$h$* in terms of *$r$

$\begin{aligned}3 \cancel{\pi} r^{2} & = & 4 \cancel{\pi} r h \\ 3 r^{\cancel{2}} & = & 4 \cancel{r} h \\ 3 r & = & 4 h \\ h & = & \frac{3}{4} r\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Now find the volume of the hemisphere in terms of *$r$

$\begin{aligned}v o l u m e_{h e m i s p h e r e} & = & \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3} \\ & = & \frac{2}{3} \pi r^{3}\end{aligned}$

> *And find the volume of the cylinder in terms of *$r$

$\begin{aligned}v o l u m e_{c y l i n d e r} & = & \pi R^{2} h \\ & = & \pi \left(2 r\right)^{2} \times \frac{3}{4} r \\ & = & \pi \cancel{4} r^{2} \times \frac{3}{\cancel{4}} r \\ & = & 3 \pi r^{3}\end{aligned}$

** correct expressions for volume of hemisphere and volume of cylinder ****[1]**

> $m$*, the scale factor for the volumes, is the volume of the cylinder divided by the volume of the hemisphere*

$\begin{aligned}m & = & \frac{3 \pi r^{3}}{\frac{2}{3} \pi r^{3}} = \frac{3 \cancel{\pi r^{3}}}{\frac{2}{3} \cancel{\pi r^{3}}} \\ & = & 3 \times \frac{3}{2} \\ & = & \frac{9}{2}\end{aligned}$

$m=\frac{9}{2}\mathrm{or}4.5$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
$ABCED$ is a five-sided shape.

![q19-4ma1-1h-qp-nov21-paper1-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/2-equations-formulae-and-identities/forming-and-solving-equations/assets/005-q19-4ma1-1h-qp-nov21-paper1-igcse-maths.png)

$ABCD$ is a rectangle. 
$CED$ is an equilateral triangle.

$AB=x\mathrm{cm}BC=y\mathrm{cm}$

The perimeter of $ABCED$is 100 cm. 
The area of $ABCED$is $R$ cm<sup>2</sup>

Show that $R = \frac{x}{4} \left(200 - \left[6 - \sqrt{3}\right] x\right)$
parts.solutionMd:
> *The length of **DE **and **CE** are both *$x$* so;*

$\mathrm{perimeter} \mathrm{of}ABCED=3x+2y$

> *Equate this to 100 and write *$y$* in terms of *$x$*.*

$\begin{aligned}3 x + 2 y & = & 100 \\ 2 y & = & 100 - 3 x \\ y & = & \frac{100 - 3 x}{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *We can now write an expression for the area of rectangle **ABCD** in terms of *$x$* *

$\begin{aligned}area A B C D & = & x y \\ & = & x \left(\frac{100 - 3 x}{2}\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Triangle **CED **is equilateral so all its internal angles are 60°. So its area is;*

$\mathrm{area}CED=\frac{1}{2}x\timesx\times\mathrm{sin}60^{\circ}$

> *It's useful to know that *$\mathrm{sin}60^{\circ}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$* (and *$\mathrm{sin}30^{\circ}=\frac{1}{2}$*) but you can also obtain the exact value of *$\mathrm{sin}60^{\circ}$* from your calculator. *

$\begin{aligned}area C E D & = & \frac{1}{2} x^{2} \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ & = & \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} x^{2}\end{aligned}$

> *Thus *$R$*, the total area of **ABCED **in terms of *$x$*, **is;*

$\begin{aligned}R & = & Area A B C D + Area C E D \\ & = & x \left(\frac{100 - 3 x}{2}\right) + \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} x^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Rewrite by factorising *$\frac{x}{4}$* out of both parts of the equation.*

$\begin{aligned}A & = & \frac{x}{4} \left(2 \left(100 - 3 x\right)\right) + \frac{x}{4} \left(\sqrt{3} x\right) \\ & = & \frac{x}{4} \left(200 - 6 x\right) + \frac{x}{4} \left(\sqrt{3} x\right)\end{aligned}$

> *                                       (note that the *$x$* lies outside the *$\sqrt{3}$*)*

> $\frac{x}{4}$* is outside both brackets so this can be simplified into one bracket using the distributive law.*

$\begin{aligned}A & = & \frac{x}{4} \left(200 - 6 x + \sqrt{3} x\right)\end{aligned}$

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a sector $OBC$ of a circle with centre $O$ and radius $(6+x)\mathrm{cm}$.

$A$ is the point on $OB$ and $D$ is the point on $OC$ such that $OA=OD=6\mathrm{cm}$

Angle $BOC=50^{\circ}$

Given that

the perimeter of sector $OBC=2\times$the perimeter of triangle $OAD$

find the value of $x$.

Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Find the perimeter of the triangle **OAD **by first using the cosine rule, *$a^{2} = b^{2} + c^{2} - 2 b c cos \left(A\right)$*.*

> *Substitute the values of the sides (both 6 cm) and angle (50°) into the cosine rule formula.*

$\begin{aligned}A D^{2} & = & 6^{2} + 6^{2} - \left(2 \times 6 \times 6 \times cos 50\right) \\ A D & = & \sqrt{ 6^{2} + 6^{2} - \left(2 \times 6 \times 6 \times cos 50\right)} \\ & = & 5 . 071419 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Find the perimeter of triangle **OAD.*

*Perimeter of ***OAD *** = 6 + 6 + 5.071419... = 17.071419... cm**<sup> </sup>*

**[1]**

> *Find the length of the arc **BC **using the formula for length of an arc *$=\frac{θ^{\circ}}{360^{\circ}}\times2πr$*.*

> * Find an expression for the length of the arc in terms of *$x$*, **by substituting *$θ=50$* and *$r=(6+x)$*.*

$B C = \frac{50}{360} \times 2 \times \pi \times \left(x + 6\right)$

**[1]**

> *Find an expression for the perimeter of the sector **OBC** in terms of *$x$*, **by adding this to 2 × the radius.*

$\begin{aligned}O B C & = & \left( \frac{50}{360} \times 2 \times \pi \times \left(x + 6\right) \right) + 2 \left(x + 6\right) \\ & = & \frac{5}{18} \left(x + 6\right) \pi + 2 \left(x + 6\right) \end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{18} \left(x + 6\right) \pi + 2 \left(x + 6\right) & = & 2 \left(17 . 071419 . . .\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify by expanding the brackets on both sides and collecting like terms.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{5 \pi}{18} x + \frac{5 \pi}{3} + 2 x + 12 & = & 34 . 14283 . . . \\ 2 . 872664 . . . x & = & 16 . 90684 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Solve the equation.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{16 . 90684 . . .}{2 . 872664 . . .} = 5 . 885422 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Round to 3 significant figures.*

$x=5.89$** cm**<sup>** **</sup>**(3 s.f.)**** [1] **
**Answers in the range 5.88 to 5.89 accepted.**

parts.problemMd:
A bowl contains $n$ pieces of fruit.

Of these, $4$ are oranges and the rest are apples.

Two pieces of fruit are going to be taken at random from the bowl.

The probability that the bowl will then contain $(n--6)$ apples is $\frac{1}{3}$

parts.solutionMd:
> *If there are **n** pieces of fruit in in total and 4 of them are oranges, then there are **n** - 4 apples to start with. *

> *If there are **n** -6 apples left after two pieces of fruit are taken, then both pieces of fruit taken must have been apples. *

> *Realising this fact is probably the trickiest part of this question!*

> *With combined probabilities 'and' usually means 'multiply'. 'Takes two apples' is the same as:*

> *     'takes an apple' (*$\frac{n-4}{n}$*) AND 'then takes another apple' (*$\frac{n-5}{n-1}$*).*

> * (Note that after taking the first apple, the numbers of pieces of fruit remaining in the bowl changes.  So the numerator and denominator must change in the second probability fraction.) Because the total probability is 1/3, those algebraic fractions multiplied together must also be equal to 1/3.*

$\frac{n-4}{n}\times\frac{n-5}{n-1}=\frac{1}{3}$

**[2]**

** ****1 mark for one correct probability fraction.  1 mark for a completely correct equation.**

> *Now rearrange into a quadratic equation you can solve.*

$\frac{ ( n - 4 ) ( n - 5 ) }{n ( n - 1 ) } = \frac{1}{3}$

$\frac{n ^{2} - 9 n + 20}{n ^{2} - n} = \frac{1}{3}$

$3 \times ( n ^{2} - 9 n + 20 ) = 1 \times ( n ^{2} - n )$

> *Now solve the quadratic equation. *

> *Here it's done by factorising, but you could also use the quadratic formula. *

> *With either method, it is easiest to start by dividing everything in the equation by 2. *

n equals space 10 space space space or space space space n space equals space 3

parts.solutionMd:

$\frac{4}{3} \pi \left(2 x\right)^{3} = \frac{1}{3} \pi \left(3 x\right)^{2} h$

$32πx^{3}=9πx^{2}h$

$\begin{aligned}32 \cancel{\pi} x^{\cancel{3}} & = & 9 \cancel{\pi} \cancel{x^{2}} h \\ 32 x & = & 9 h\end{aligned}$

parts.problemMd: Solve      $\frac{4x-1}{5}+\frac{x+4}{2}=3$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Remove the fractions by multiplying every term by the lowest common denominator. *

> *The lowest common denominator is the LCM of 5 and 2 = 10*

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify by cancelling each fraction. *

> *The fractions should disappear.*

> *Expand both sets of brackets on the left-hand side. *

$\begin{aligned}8 x - 2 + 5 x + 20 & = & 30\end{aligned}$

> *Simplify the left hand side by bringing the **x** terms together and the number terms together.*

$\begin{aligned}8 x + 5 x - 2 + 20 & = & 30 \\ 13 x + 18 & = & 30\end{aligned}$

> *Subtract 18 from both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}13 x & = & 30 - 18 \\ 13 x & = & 12\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 13.*

$x=\frac{12}{13}$

$x=\frac{12}{13}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Solve                $\frac{x+1}{3}+\frac{2x+5}{4}=2$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Remove the fractions by multiplying every term by the lowest common denominator. *

> *The lowest common denominator is the LCM of 3 and 4 = 12*

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify by cancelling each fraction. *

> *The fractions should disappear.*

$\begin{aligned}\cancel{12} \left(\frac{x + 1}{\cancel{3}}\right) + \cancel{ 12} \left(\frac{2 x + 5}{\cancel{4}}\right) & = & 12 \left(2\right) \\ 4 \left(x + 1\right) + 3 \left(2 x + 5\right) & = & 24\end{aligned}$

> *Expand both sets of brackets on the left-hand side. *

> *Remember to expand both parts of the bracket.*

$\begin{aligned}4 x + 4 + 6 x + 15 & = & 24\end{aligned}$

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify the left hand side by bringing the **x** terms together and the number terms together.*

$\begin{aligned}4 x + 6 x + 4 + 15 & = & 24 \\ 10 x + 19 & = & 24\end{aligned}$

> *Subtract 19 from both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}10 x & = & 24 - 19 \\ 10 x & = & 5\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 10.*

$x=\frac{5}{10}=\frac{1}{2}$

$x=\frac{1}{2}$ **[1] **

**0.5 also accepted**

parts.problemMd: Solve    $\frac{x+2}{3x}+\frac{x-2}{2x}=3$

$\begin{aligned}6 x \left(\frac{x + 2}{3 x}\right) + 6 x \left(\frac{x - 2}{2 x}\right) & = & 6 x \left(3\right)\end{aligned}$

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify by cancelling the common terms in each fraction. *

> *The fractions should disappear.*

$\begin{aligned}\cancel{6 x} \left(\frac{x + 2}{\cancel{3 x}}\right) + \cancel{6 x} \left(\frac{x - 2}{\cancel{2 x}}\right) & = & 6 x \left(3\right) \\ 2 \left(x + 2\right) + 3 \left(x - 2\right) & = & 18 x\end{aligned}$

> *Expand both sets of brackets on the left-hand side. *

> *Remember to expand both parts of the bracket.*

$\begin{aligned}2 x + 4 + 3 x - 6 & = & 18 x\end{aligned}$

> *Simplify the left hand side by bringing the **x** terms together and the number terms together.*

$\begin{aligned}2 x + 3 x + 4 - 6 & = & 18 x \\ 5 x - 2 & = & 18 x\end{aligned}$

> *Bring the **x** terms to one side by subtracting 5**x** from both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}- 2 & = & 18 x - 5 x \\ 13 x & = & - 2\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 13.*

$x=\frac{-2}{13}$

$x=-\frac{2}{13}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Solve   $\frac{h+7}{3}+\frac{2h-1}{2}=\frac{5}{6}$

$\begin{aligned}2 h + 14 + 6 h - 3 & = & 5\end{aligned}$

> *Simplify the left hand side by bringing the **h** terms together and the number terms together.*

$\begin{aligned}2 h + 6 h + 14 - 3 & = & 5 \\ 8 h + 11 & = & 5\end{aligned}$

> *Subtract 11 from both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}8 h & = & 5 - 11 \\ 8 h & = & - 6\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

parts.problemMd: Solve   $\frac{3x-2}{4}-\frac{2x+5}{3}=\frac{1-x}{6}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Remove the fractions by multiplying every term by the lowest common denominator. *

> *The lowest common denominator is the LCM of 4, 3 and 6 = 12.*

$\begin{aligned}12 \left(\frac{3 x - 2}{4}\right) - 12 \left(\frac{2 x + 5}{3}\right) & = & 12 \left(\frac{1 - x}{6}\right)\end{aligned}$

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify by cancelling the common terms in each fraction. The fractions should disappear.*

$\begin{aligned}\cancel{12} \left(\frac{3 x - 2}{\cancel{4}}\right) - \cancel{12} \left(\frac{2 x + 5}{\cancel{3}}\right) & = & \cancel{12} \left(\frac{1 - x}{\cancel{6}}\right) \\ 3 \left(3 x - 2\right) - 4 \left(2 x + 5\right) & = & 2 \left(1 - x\right)\end{aligned}$

* ***[1]**

> *Expand all three sets of brackets. *

> *Remember to expand both parts of the bracket and be careful with the negative sign.*

$\begin{aligned}9 x - 6 - 8 x - 20 & = & 2 - 2 x\end{aligned}$

> *Simplify the left hand side.*

$\begin{aligned}9 x - 8 x - 6 - 20 & = & 2 - 2 x \\ x - 26 & = & 2 - 2 x\end{aligned}$

> *Bring the **x** terms to one side by adding 2**x** to both sides and the number terms to the other by adding 26 to both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}x - 26 & = & 2 - 2 x \\ + 2 x & = & + 2 x \\ 3 x - 26 & = & 2 \\ + 26 & = & + 26 \\ 3 x & = & 28\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 3.*

$x=\frac{28}{3}$

$x=9\frac{1}{3}$ **[1]**

**The improper fraction is also accepted. **

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify by cancelling each fraction. The fractions should disappear.*

$\begin{aligned}\cancel{20} \left(\frac{9 a - 7}{\cancel{5}}\right) - \cancel{20} \left(\frac{3 a - 7}{\cancel{4}}\right) & = & 20 \left(4 . 55\right) \\ 4 \left(9 a - 7\right) - 5 \left(3 a - 7\right) & = & 91\end{aligned}$

> *Expand both sets of brackets on the left-hand side. *

> *Remember to expand both terms inside each bracket and take care with the "double negative" −5 × −7*

$\begin{aligned}36 a - 28 - 15 a + 35 & = & 91\end{aligned}$

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify the left hand side by bringing the **x** terms together and the number terms together.*

$\begin{aligned}36 a - 15 a - 28 + 35 & = & 91 \\ 21 a + 7 & = & 91\end{aligned}$

> *Subtract 7 from both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}21 a & = & 84\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$a=\frac{84}{21}=4$

$a=4$ **[1]**

> *Expand both sets of brackets on the left-hand side. *

> *Remember to expand both terms inside each bracket and take care with the "double negative" in the second bracket (−3 × −3)*

$\begin{aligned}16 - 4 x - 6 x + 9 & = & 24\end{aligned}$

* ***[1]**

> *Simplify the left hand side by bringing the **x** terms together and the number terms together.*

$\begin{aligned}16 + 9 - 4 x - 6 x & = & 24 \\ 25 - 10 x & = & 24\end{aligned}$

> *Subtract 25 from both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}- 10 x & = & - 1\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by -10.*

$x=\frac{-1}{-10}=\frac{1}{10}$

$x=\frac{1}{10}$ **[1]**

**0.1 also accepted**

parts.problemMd:
The functions $f$and $g$ are defined as

$\begin{aligned}f \left(x\right)  & = &  x^{2}  +  6  \\ g \left(x\right)  & = &  x  –  10\end{aligned}$

Solve the equation $\mathrm{fg}(x)=f(x)$

Show clear algebraic working.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Although this may at first appear to be a quadratic equations question, it's actually a linear equations question "in disguise"!*

> *First rewrite *$fg \left(x\right) = f \left(x\right)$* in terms of *$x$* using composite functions.*

$\left(x - 10\right)^{2} + 6 = x^{2} + 6$

**[1]**

> *Expand the brackets; *$\left(x - 10\right)^{2} = \left(x - 10\right) \left(x - 10\right)$*.*

$x^{2}-20x+100+6=x^{2}+6$

**[1]**

> *Collect like terms on the left hand side.*

$x^{2}-20x+106=x^{2}+6$

> *Now subtract *$x^{2}$* from both sides, to reveal the linear equation!*

$\begin{aligned}x^{2} - 20 x + 106 & = & x^{2} + 6 \\ - x^{2} & = & - x^{2} \\ - 20 x + 106 & = & 6\end{aligned}$

> *Subtract 106 from both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}- 20 x & = & - 100\end{aligned}$

> *And divide both sides by -20.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{- 100}{- 20} = 5\end{aligned}$

$x=5$ ** [1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 5, remember to apply this to every term*

$15 \left(x - 4\right) + \left(x + 2\right) = 30$

**[1]**

> *Expand the bracket on the left*

$15 x - 60 + \left(x + 2\right) = 30$

> *Simplify the left*

$16x-58=30$

**[1]**

> *Add 58 to both sides*

$16x=88$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 16*

$x=\frac{88}{16}=\frac{11}{2}=5.5$

$x=5.5$ **[1]**

**Or as a fraction **$\frac{11}{2}$

parts.problemMd:
Make $h$ the subject of the formula

$t=\frac{gh}{10}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Get **gh **on its own (by multiplying both sides by 10)*

$10t=gh$

**[1]**

> *Get **h** on its own (by dividing both sides by **g**)  *

$\frac{10t}{g}=h$

$h=\frac{10t}{g}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Make $t$ the subject of the formula $w=3t+11$
parts.solutionMd:
*Get 3**t** on its own (by subtracting 11 from both sides)* * *

$w-11=3t$

**[1]**

> *Get **t** on its own (by dividing both sides by 3)  *

$\frac{w-11}{3}=t$

$t=\frac{w-11}{3}$**[1]**

parts.problemMd: Make $t$ the subject of the formula $y=\frac{t}{3}-2a$
parts.solutionMd:
*Get *$\frac{t}{3}$* on its own (by adding 2**a** to both sides)* * *

$y+2a=\frac{t}{3}$

**[1]**

> *Get **t** on its own (by multiplying both sides by 3)  *

$3 \left(y + 2 a\right) = t$

$t=3(y+2a)$* ***[1]**

$t=3y+6a$** is also accepted**

parts.problemMd: Make $F$ the subject of the formula  $C  =  \frac{5 \left(F  -  32\right)}{9}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Get 5(**F** - 32) on its own (by multiplying both sides by 9)* * *

$9 C = 5 \left(F - 32\right)$

**[1]**

*Method 1*

*Get **F** - 32 on its own (by dividing both sides by 5)* * *

$\frac{9C}{5}=F-32$

**[1]**

> *Get **F** on its own (by adding 32 to both sides)  *

$\frac{9C}{5}+32=F$

$F=\frac{9C}{5}+32$* ***[1]**

*Method 2*

*Expand the brackets* * *

$9C=5F-160$ * *

*Get 5**F** on its own (by adding 160 to both sides)* * *

$9C+160=5F$

**[1]**

> *Get **F** on its own (by dividing both sides by 5)  *

$\frac{9C+160}{5}=F$

$F=\frac{9C+160}{5}$** [1]**

**either answers from Method 1 or Method 2 are accepted**

parts.problemMd: Make $t$ the subject of the formula $p=at--d$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Isolate the term involving **t** first, the **at** term by adding **d** to both sides.*

$p+d=at$

**[1]**

> *Isolate **t** by dividing both sides by **a**.*

$\frac{p+d}{a}=t$

$\thereforet=\frac{p+d}{a}$* ***[1]**

**Equivalent expressions allowed such as **$t=\frac{p}{a}+\frac{d}{a}$**.**

parts.problemMd: Make $a$ the subject of $d=g+2ac$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Isolate the term involving **a** first, the 2**ac** term by subtracting **g** from both sides.*

$d-g=2ac$

**[1]**

> *Isolate **a** by dividing both sides by 2**c**.*

$\frac{d-g}{2c}=a$

$\thereforea=\frac{d-g}{2c}$* ***[1]**

**Equivalent expressions allowed such as **$a=\frac{d}{2c}-\frac{g}{2c}$**.**

parts.problemMd: Make $a$ the subject of the formula $M=ac--bd$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Isolate the term involving **a** first, the **ac** term by adding **bd** to both sides.*

$M+bd=ac$

**[1]**

> *Isolate **a** by dividing both sides by **c**.*

$\frac{M+bd}{c}=a$

$\thereforea=\frac{M+bd}{c}$* ***[1]**

**Equivalent expressions allowed such as **$a=\frac{M}{c}+\frac{bd}{c}$**.**

parts.problemMd: Make $e$ the subject of the formula $h=3e+f$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Isolate the term involving **e** first, the **3e** term by subtracting **f** from both sides.*

$h-f=3e$

**[1]**

> *Isolate **e** by dividing both sides by 3.*

$\frac{h-f}{3}=e$

$\thereforee=\frac{h-f}{3}$* ***[1]**

**Equivalent expressions allowed such as **$e = \frac{1}{3} \left(h - f\right)$**.**

parts.problemMd: Make $t$ the subject of        $c=t^{3}-8v$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Isolate the term involving **t** first, the **t*<sup>*3*</sup>* term by adding 8**v** to both sides.*

$c+8v=t^{3}$

**[1]**

> *Isolate **t** by taking the cube root of both sides.*

$\sqrt[3]{c + 8 v} = t$

$\therefore \mathbf{\mathit{t}} = \sqrt[3]{\mathbf{c} + 8 \mathbf{v}}$* ***[1]**

**Equivalent expressions allowed such as **$t = \left(c + 8 v\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}$**.**

parts.problemMd:
Rearrange$y=3x--2$ to make x the subject.

Circle your answer.

| $x=\frac{y}{3}-2$ | $x=\frac{y+2}{3}$ | $x=\frac{y-2}{3}$ | $x=\frac{y}{3}+2$ |
|---|---|---|---|
parts.solutionMd:
> *Add 2 to both sides of the equation.*

$y+2=3x$

> *Divide both sides by 3.*

$\frac{y+2}{3}=x$

$x=\frac{y+2}{3}$ **[1]**

> *If you divide the left hand side by 3, then subtract 2 from both sides, you get the incorrect answer of *$x=\frac{y}{3}-2$*.*

> *If you subtract 2 from both sides, then divide both sides by 3, you get the incorrect answer of *$x=\frac{y-2}{3}$*.*

> *If you divide the left hand side by 3, then add 2 to both sides you get the incorrect answer of *$x=\frac{y}{3}+2$*.*

parts.problemMd: Rearrange $v=u+at$  to make $t$ the subject of the formula.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Start by subtracting **u** from both sides.*

$v-u=at$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by **a**.*

$\frac{v-u}{a}=t$

$\thereforet=\frac{v-u}{a}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Rearrange this formula to make *y* the subject.

*x* = *y*<sup>2 </sup>+ 7
parts.solutionMd:
> *Subtract 7 from both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}x - 7 & = & y^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *It may be easier here to swap the left and right sides, although it is not necessary.*

$\begin{aligned}y^{2} & = & x - 7 \end{aligned}$

> *Take the square root of both sides, remember that a square root can be both positive or negative.*

$\begin{aligned} y^{2} & = & x - 7 \\ \sqrt{} & = & \sqrt{} \\ y & = & \pm \sqrt{x - 7}\end{aligned}$

$y=\pm\sqrt{x-7}$** [1]**

** ± sign not necessary for full marks**

> *Isolate the term involving **x** by adding 3 to both sides of the equation.*

$y+3=7x$

**[1]**

> *Isolate x by dividing boths sides by 7.*

$\frac{y+3}{7}=x$

$x=\frac{y+3}{7}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Make $y$ the subject of the formula    $p=\sqrt{\frac{x+y}{5}}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Remove the square-root sign (by squaring both sides)* * *

$p^{2}=\frac{x+y}{5}$

**[1]**

*Get **x** + **y** on its own (by multiplying both sides by 5)* * *

$5p^{2}=x+y$

**[1]**

*Get **y** on its own (by subtracting **x** from both sides)* * *

$5p^{2}-x=y$

$y=5p^{2}-x$** [1]**

parts.problemMd: Make $t$the subject of the formula   $2 \left(d - t\right)  =  4 t  + 7$
parts.solutionMd:
*Expand the brackets (by multiplying the terms inside by 2)* * *

$2d-2t=4t+7$ * *

*Get the **t** terms on one side (for example, by adding 2**t** to both sides and collecting "like" terms)* * *

$2d=4t+7+2t\,2d=6t+7$

**[1]**

*Get 6**t** on its own (by subtracting 7 from both sides)* * *

$2d-7=6t$

**[1]**

*Get **t** on its own (by dividing both sides by 6)* * *

$\frac{2d-7}{6}=t$

$t=\frac{2d-7}{6}$* ***[1]**

$t=\frac{7-2d}{-6}$** is also accepted**

parts.problemMd: Make $m$ the subject of the formula      $v=\sqrt{\frac{2E}{m}}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Remove the square-root sign (by squaring both sides)* * *

$v^{2}=\frac{2E}{m}$

**[1]**

*Move **m** out of the denominator (by multiplying both sides by **m**)* * *

$mv^{2}=2E$

**[1]**

> *Get **m** on its own (by dividing both sides by **v*<sup>*2*</sup>*)*

$m=\frac{2E}{v^{2}}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Make $p$ the subject of the formula     $y=3p^{2}-4$
parts.solutionMd:
*Get 3**p*<sup>*2*</sup>* on its own (by adding 4 to both sides)* * *

$y+4=3p^{2}$

**[1]**

*Get **p*<sup>*2*</sup>* on its own (by dividing both sides by 3)* * *

$\frac{y+4}{3}=p^{2}$ * *

*Get **p **on its own (by taking square roots of both sides and writing ±)* * *

$\pm\sqrt{\frac{y+4}{3}}=p$

**attempt to square root ****[1]**

$p=\pm\sqrt{\frac{y+4}{3}}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
$m=\sqrt{\frac{k+1}{4}}$

Make $k$ the subject of the formula.
parts.solutionMd:
*Remove the square-root sign (by squaring both sides)* * *

$m^{2}=\frac{k+1}{4}$

**[1]**

*Get **k** + 1 on its own (by multiplying both sides by 4)* * *

$4m^{2}=k+1$

**[1]**

*Get **k** on its own (by subtracting 1 from both sides)* * *

$4m^{2}-1=k$

$k=4m^{2}-1$** [1]**

parts.problemMd: Make $m$the subject of   $g-3m=am+5$
parts.solutionMd:
*Get the **m** terms on to one side (for example, by adding 3**m** to both sides)* * *

$g=am+5+3m$ * *

*Get the **m** terms on their own (by subtracting 5 from both sides)* * *

$g-5=am+3m$

**[1]**

*am** and 3**m** are not "like" terms* *Factorise **m** out of these two terms* * *

$g - 5 = m \left(a + 3\right)$

**[1]**

*Get **m** on its own (by dividing both sides by **a** + 3)* * *

$\frac{g-5}{a+3}=m$

$m=\frac{g-5}{a+3}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Make $c$ the subject of $A=\frac{c}{y}-5z$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Isolate the term involving **c** first, the *$\frac{c}{y}$* term by adding 5**z** to both sides.*

$A+5z=\frac{c}{y}$

**[1]**

> *Isolate **c** by multiplying both sides by **y**.*

$y \left(A + 5 z\right) = c$

$\thereforec=y(A+5z)$* ***[1]**

**Equivalent expressions allowed such as **$c=Ay+5yz$**.**

parts.problemMd: Make $f$ the subject of $m=\sqrt{\frac{1}{3}ef}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Isolate the term involving **f**, the *$\frac{1}{3}ef$* term, by squaring both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}m^{2} & = & \frac{1}{3} e f\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 3.*

$3m^{2}=ef$

> *Isolate **f** by dividing both sides by **e**.*

$\frac{3m^{2}}{e}=f$

$\thereforef=\frac{3m^{2}}{e}$* ***[1]**

**Equivalent expressions allowed such as **$f=3m^{2}e^{-1}$**.**

parts.problemMd: Make $g$ the subject of $k=ag^{2}$
parts.solutionMd:
Divide both sides by a to get

$\frac{k}{a}=g^{2}$

**[M1]**

Square root both sides

$g=\pm\sqrt{\frac{k}{a}}$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: Correct first step. You can get this mark for taking the square root of both sides if you write $\sqrt{k}=\sqrt{a}g$.
> 
> **A1**: Correct answer. You do not need the ± symbol for the mark.

parts.problemMd:
Rearrange $y=\sqrt{w^{3}}$ to make $w$ the subject.

Circle your answer.

| $w=y^{6}$ | $w  = \sqrt[3]{y^{2}}$ | $w=\sqrt{y^{3}}$ | $w=y^{5}$ |
|---|---|---|---|
parts.solutionMd:
> *Square both sides of the equation.*

$y^{2}=w^{3}$

> *Take the cube root of both sides.*

$\sqrt[3]{y^{2}} = w$

$\mathbf{\mathit{w}} = \sqrt[3]{\mathbf{\mathit{y}}^{2}}$ **[1]**

> *If you square both sides and then multiply the powers together on the *$y$*, you will get the incorrect answer of *$w=y^{6}$*.*

> *If you copy the operations that are initially acting on the *$w$* (cube and square root) and copy them on to the *$y$* instead, you will get the incorrect answer of *$w=\sqrt{y^{3}}$*.*

> *If you square both sides and then add the powers together on the *$y$*, you will get the incorrect answer of *$w=y^{5}$*.*

parts.problemMd: Rearrange  $a=\frac{b}{c}+5$  to make $c$ the subject.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Start by subtracting 5 from both sides to isolate the term involving **c**.*

$a-5=\frac{b}{c}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by c to remove the fraction.*

$c \left(a - 5\right) = b$

**[1]**

> *To make **c** the subject, divide both sides by (**a** - 5).*

$c=\frac{b}{a-5}$

$c=\frac{b}{a-5}$ **[1]**

**Ensure that " ****c**** = " is included in your final answer to gain full marks.**

parts.problemMd:
Use the formula $s=ut+\frac{1}{2}at^{2}$.

Make $a$ the subject of the formula.

$a$ = ..................
parts.solutionMd:
> *Isolate the term involving **a **by subtracting **ut** from both sides of the formula.*

$s-ut=\frac{1}{2}at^{2}$

> *Remove the fraction by multiplying both sides by its denominator, 2.*

$2 \left(s - u t\right) = a t^{2}$

**[1]**

> *Finally, to isolate **a**, divide both sides by **t*<sup>*2*</sup>*.*

$\frac{2 \left(s - u t\right)}{t^{2}} = a$

$a=\frac{2(s-ut)}{t^{2}}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Make $t$ the subject of $s=\frac{1}{2}at^{2}$
parts.solutionMd:
> **[exam-tip]**
> 'Make t the subject' means to rearrange the given formula so that it begins with  $t=$

> *Rearrange the formula, using the balance method and doing the same thing to both sides of the equation at each step*

> *The inverse of *$\frac{1}{2}$* is to multiply both sides by 2 giving:*

$\begin{aligned}s & = & \frac{1}{2} a t^{2} \\ 2 s & = & a t^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[M1]**

> *Divide both sides by *$a$

$\begin{aligned}\frac{2 s}{a} & = & t^{2}\end{aligned}$

> *Square root both sides*

$\begin{aligned}\pm \sqrt{\frac{2 s}{a}} & = & t\end{aligned}$

$t=\pm\sqrt{\frac{2s}{a}}$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: Awarded for a correct first step in rearranging the formula. E.g. $2s=at^{2}$ or $\frac{s}{a}=\frac{1}{2}t^{2}$ or $\frac{2s}{a}=t^{2}$
> 
> **A1**: This mark is still awarded with $\pm$ omitted in final answer.

parts.problemMd:
Make $y$ the subject of the formula

$t=\frac{2-3y}{y+2}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Remove the fraction (by multiplying both sides by **y** + 2)* * *

$t \left(y + 2\right) = 2 - 3 y$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets (by multiplying the terms inside by **t**)* * *

$ty+2t=2-3y$ * *

*Collect the **y** terms on one side (for example, by adding 3**y** to both sides then subtracting 2**t **from both sides)* * *

$\begin{aligned}t y + 2 t + 3 y & = & 2 \\ t y + 3 y & = & 2 - 2 t\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

*Factorise** y** out of the terms on the left* * *

$y \left(t + 3\right) = 2 - 2 t$

**[1]**

*Get y on its own (by dividing both sides by **t** + 3)* * *

$y=\frac{2-2t}{t+3}$* ***[1]**

$y=\frac{2t-2}{-t-3}$** is also accepted**

parts.problemMd: Make $v$ the subject of the formula $w  =  \frac{15 \left(t  -  2 v\right)}{v}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Remove fractions (by multiplying both sides by **v**)* * *

$w v = 15 \left(t - 2 v\right)$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets (by multiplying the terms inside by 15)* * *

$wv=15t-30v$ * *

*Move the **v** terms to one side (for example, by adding 30**v** to both sides)* * *

$wv+30v=15t$ * *

*Factorise **v** out of the terms on the left* * *

$v \left(w + 30\right) = 15 t$

**[1]**

> *Get **v** on its own (by dividing both sides by **w** + 30)*

$v=\frac{15t}{w+30}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Make $a$ the subject of       $a+3=\frac{2a+7}{r}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Remove fractions (by multiplying both sides by **r**)* * *

$r \left(a + 3\right) = 2 a + 7$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets (by multiplying the terms inside by **r**)* * *

$ra+3r=2a+7$ * *

*Move the **a** terms to one side (for example, by subtracting 2**a** from both sides)* * *

$ra+3r-2a=7$ * *

*Get the **a** terms on their own (by subtracting 3**r** from both sides)* * *

$ra-2a=7-3r$ * *

*Factorise **a** out of the terms on the left* * *

$a \left(r - 2\right) = 7 - 3 r$

**[1]**

> *Get **a** on its own (by dividing both sides by **r **- 2)*

$a=\frac{7-3r}{r-2}$* ***[1]**

$a=\frac{3r-7}{2-r}$** is also accepted**

parts.problemMd:
$m=\sqrt{\frac{k^{3}+1}{4}}$

Make $k$ the subject of the formula.
parts.solutionMd:
*Remove the square-root sign (by squaring both sides)* * *

$m^{2}=\frac{k^{3}+1}{4}$

**[1]**

*Remove fractions (by multiplying both sides by 4)* * *

$4m^{2}=k^{3}+1$ * *

*Get **k*<sup>*3*</sup>* on its own (by subtracting 1 from both sides)* * *

$4m^{2}-1=k^{3}$ * *

*Get **k** on its own (by cube-rooting both sides)* * *

$\sqrt[3]{4 m^{2} - 1} = k$

**attempting to cube root**** [1]**

$\mathbf{\mathit{k}} = \sqrt[3]{4 \mathbf{\mathit{m}}^{2} - 1}$** [1]**

parts.problemMd: Make $a$ the subject of the formula  $p=\frac{3a+5}{4-a}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Remove fractions (by multiplying both sides by (4 - **a**)* * *

$p \left(4 - a\right) = 3 a + 5$

**[1]**

*Expanding the brackets (by multiplying each term inside by **p**)* * *

$4p-pa=3a+5$ * *

*Get the **a** terms on one side (for example, by adding **pa** to both sides then subtracting 5 from both sides)* * *

$\begin{aligned}4 p & = & 3 a + 5 + a p \\ 4 p - 5 & = & 3 a + a p\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

*Factorise **a** out of the terms on the right* * *

$4 p - 5 = a \left(3 + p\right)$

**[1]**

*Get **a** on its own (by dividing both sides by 3 + **p**)* * *

$\frac{4p-5}{3+p}=a$

$a=\frac{4p-5}{3+p}$* ***[1]**

$a=\frac{5-4p}{-3-p}$* ***is also accepted**

parts.problemMd:
Make $t$ the subject of the formula

$p=\frac{3-2t}{4+t}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Remove fractions (by multiplying both sides by 4 + **t**)* * *

$p \left(4 + t\right) = 3 - 2 t$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets (by multiplying each term inside by **p**)* * *

$4p+pt=3-2t$ * *

*Move the **t** terms to one side (for example, by adding 2**t** to both sides then subtracting 4**p** from both sides)* * *

$\begin{aligned}4 p + p t + 2 t & = & 3 \\ p t + 2 t & = & 3 - 4 p\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

*Factorise **t** out of the terms on the left* * *

$t \left(p + 2\right) = 3 - 4 p$

**[1]**

> *Get **t** on its own (by dividing both sides by** p** + 2)*

$t=\frac{3-4p}{p+2}$* ***[1]**

$t=\frac{4p-3}{-p-2}$** is also accepted**

parts.problemMd:
Make $m$ the subject of

$\frac{m}{v}-\frac{t}{b}=\frac{m-t}{R}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Get rid of fractions (by multiplying both sides by **bvR**)* * *

$\begin{aligned}b v R \left(\frac{m}{v} - \frac{t}{b}\right) & = & b v R \times \frac{\left(m - t\right)}{R} \\ & & \\ \frac{b \cancel{v} R m}{\cancel{v}} - \frac{\cancel{b} v R t}{\cancel{b}} & = & \frac{b v \cancel{R} \left(m - t\right)}{\cancel{R}} \\ & & \\ b R m - v R t & = & b v \left(m - t\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets on the right* * *

$bRm-vRt=bvm-bvt$ * *

*Move all the **m** terms on to one side (for example, by subtracting **bvm** from both sides then adding **vRt** to both sides)* * *

$\begin{aligned}b R m - v R t - b v m & = & - b v t \\ b R m - b v m & = & v R t - b v t\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

*Factorise **m** out of the terms on the left* * *

$m \left(b R - b v\right) = v R t - b v t$

**[1]**

> *Get **m** on its own (by dividing both sides by **bR - bv**)*

$m=\frac{vRt-bvt}{bR-bv}$* ***[1]**

$m=\frac{bvt-vRt}{bv-bR}$* ***is also accepted**

parts.problemMd: Make $m$ the subject of the formula  $f=\frac{3m+4}{m-1}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Remove fractions (by multiplying both sides by **m** - 1)* * *

$f \left(m - 1\right) = 3 m + 4$

**[1]**

*Expand the brackets (by multiplying each term inside by **f**)* * *

$fm-f=3m+4$ * *

*Get all the **m** terms on one side (for example, by subtracting 3**m** from both sides then adding **f **to both sides)* * *

$\begin{aligned}f m - f - 3 m & = & 4 \\ f m - 3 m & = & 4 + f\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

*Factorise **m** out of the terms on the left* * *

$m \left(f - 3\right) = 4 + f$

*Get **m** on its own (by dividing both sides by **f** - 3)* * *

$m=\frac{4+f}{f-3}$* ***[1]**

$m=\frac{-f-4}{3-f}$** is also accepted**

parts.problemMd: Make *t *the subject of  $n^{2}=\frac{4d+t^{3}}{t^{3}}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Remove fractions (by multiplying both sides by **t*<sup>*3*</sup>*)* * *

$t^{3}n^{2}=4d+t^{3}$

**[1]**

*Collect all the terms in **t** on one side (subtract **t*<sup>*3*</sup>* from both sides)* * *

$t^{3}n^{2}-t^{3}=4d$ * *

*'Factorise out' the the **t*<sup>*3*</sup> * *

$\begin{aligned}t^{3} \left(n^{2} - 1\right) & = & 4 d\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

*And divide both sides by '**n*<sup>*2*</sup>* − 1' to leave **t*<sup>*3*</sup>* on its own on the left hand side* * *

$\begin{aligned}t^{3} & = & \frac{4 d}{n^{2} - 1}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

*Take the cube root of both sides* * *

$\mathbf{\mathit{t}} = \sqrt[3]{\frac{4 \mathbf{\mathit{d}}}{\mathbf{\mathit{n}}^{2} - 1}}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Make $c$ the subject of the formula  $p=\sqrt{\frac{ac+8}{3+c}}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Start by squaring both sides to remove the square root.*

$p^{2}=\frac{ac+8}{3+c}$

**[1]**

> *Remove fractions by multiplying (both sides) by 3 + **c.*

$p^{2} \left(3 + c\right) = a c + 8$

> *Expand the brackets by multiplying each term inside by p*<sup>*2*</sup>*. *

$3p^{2}+cp^{2}=ac+8$

**[1]**

*Being all the **c** terms to one side (for example, by subtracting **ac** from both sides then adding 3**p*<sup>*2*</sup>* **to both sides)* * *

$\begin{aligned}3 p^{2} + c p^{2} - a c & = & 8 \\ c p^{2} - a c & = & 8 - 3 p^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

*Factorise **c** from the terms on the left-hand side.* * *

$c \left(p^{2} - a\right) = 8 - 3 p^{2}$

> *Isolate **c** by dividing (both sides) by **p*<sup>*2*</sup>* - a.*

$c=\frac{8-3p^{2}}{p^{2}-a}$

*There is nothing to simplify or rearrange so this is the final answer.* * *

$c=\frac{8-3p^{2}}{p^{2}-a}$* ***[1]**

**Equivalent expressions allowed such as **$c=\frac{3p^{2}-8}{a-p^{2}}$**.**

parts.problemMd: Make $x$the subject of $y=\sqrt{\frac{x+1}{x-4}}$
parts.solutionMd:
*Remove the square root by squaring both sides.* * *

$y^{2}=\frac{x+1}{x-4}$

**[1]**

*Remove the fraction by multiplying both sides by the denominator (**x** - 4).* * *

$y^{2} \left(x - 4\right) = x + 1$

**[1]*** *

> *Expand the brackets on the left hand side of the formula.*

$\begin{aligned}x y^{2} - 4 y^{2} & = & x + 1\end{aligned}$

> *Collect x terms on the same side of the formula - and everything else on the other side (by subtracting **x** from, and adding 4**y*<sup>*2*</sup>* to, both sides)*

$xy^{2}-x=4y^{2}+1$

**[1]**

*Factorise **x** out of the terms on the left hand side* * *

$x \left(y^{2} - 1\right) = 4 y^{2} + 1$

*Get **x** on its own (by dividing both sides by **y*<sup>*2*</sup>* - 1)* * *

$x=\frac{4y^{2}+1}{y^{2}-1}$

$x=\frac{4y^{2}+1}{y^{2}-1}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Given that $n>0$ make $n$ the subject of the formula $y=\frac{n^{2}+d}{n^{2}}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Remove the fraction by multiplying both sides by the denominator (**n*<sup>*2*</sup>*).*

$yn^{2}=n^{2}+d$

**[1]*** *

> *Collect **n** terms on the same side of the formula (by subtracting **n*<sup>*2*</sup>* from both sides).*

$yn^{2}-n^{2}=d$

**[1]**

> *Factorise **n*<sup>*2*</sup>* out of the terms on the left hand side.*

$n^{2} \left(y - 1\right) = d$

**[1]**

> *Get **n*<sup>*2*</sup>* on its own (by dividing both sides by **y** - 1).*

$n^{2}=\frac{d}{y-1}$

> *Now square root, but we are given that *$n>0$* so we only need the positive square root.*

$n=\sqrt{\frac{d}{y-1}}$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd: Rearrange $y=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x+1}}$ to make $x$ the subject.
parts.solutionMd:
> *First square both sides of the formula to remove the square root.*

$\begin{aligned}y^{2} & = & \left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x + 1}}\right)^{2} \\ y^{2} & = & \frac{\left(1\right)^{2}}{\left(\sqrt{x + 1}\right)^{2}} \\ y^{2} & = & \frac{1}{x + 1}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by the denominator to remove the fraction.*

$y^{2} \left(x + 1\right) = 1$

**[1]**

> *Expand the brackets on the left-hand side.*

$xy^{2}+y^{2}=1$

> *Isolate the **x** term by subtracting **y*<sup>*2*</sup>* from both sides.*

$xy^{2}=1-y^{2}$

> *Finally divide both sides by **y*<sup>*2*</sup>* to make **x** the subject.*

$x=\frac{1-y^{2}}{y^{2}}$

$x=\frac{1-y^{2}}{y^{2}}$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd: Make $e$ the subject of $w=\sqrt{\frac{e+g}{ef-d}}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Square both sides*

$\begin{aligned}w & = & \sqrt{\frac{e + g}{e f - d}} \\ w^{2} & = & \frac{e + g}{e f - d}\end{aligned}$

**[M1]**

> *Multiply by the denominator and expand the brackets*

$\begin{aligned}w^{2} \left(e f - d\right) & = & e + g \\ e f w^{2} - d w^{2} & = & e + g\end{aligned}$

**[M1]**

> *Rearrange to have all the terms containing *$e$* on one side*

$\begin{aligned}e f w^{2} - d w^{2} - e & = & g \\ e f w^{2} - e & = & g + d w^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[M1]**

> *Take out a factor of *$e$* on the left side*

$e \left(f w^{2} - 1\right) = g + d w^{2}$

> *Divide by the term in the brackets to leave *$e$* on the left*

$e=\frac{g+dw^{2}}{fw^{2}-1}$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **A1**: If you rearrange to put all the $e$ terms on the right hand side earlier in your method, you may have one of the following equivalent versions of this answer:
> 
> $e=\frac{-g-dw^{2}}{1-fw^{2}}\mathrm{or}e=-\frac{g+dw^{2}}{1-fw^{2}}$
> 
> One of these will also get the marks.

parts.problemMd: Make $n$ the subject of the formula $x=\frac{3p+n}{3n-4}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Remove the fraction by multiplying both sides by the denominator*

$x \left(3 n - 4\right) = 3 p + n$

> *Expand the brackets*

$3nx-4x=3p+n$

**[M1]**

> *Collect the *$n$* terms on one side by subtracting *$n$* from both sides*

$3nx-n-4x=3p$

> *Move any other terms to the other side by using the inverse operation*

> *Add *$4x$* to both sides*

$3nx-n=3p+4x$

**[M1]**

> *Take out a factor of *$n$

$n \left(3 x - 1\right) = 3 p + 4 x$

> *Divide by the bracket to leave *$n$* as the subject*

$n=\frac{3p+4x}{3x-1}$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> You must have "$n=$" as part of your final answer.

parts.problemMd:
Solve the simultaneous equations

$4x+y=25$
 $x---3y=16$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Number the equations.*

> $\begin{aligned}4 x + y & = & 25 \left(1\right) \\ x - 3 y & = & 16 \left(2\right)\end{aligned}$* *

> *Make the **y** terms equal by multiplying all parts of equation (1) by 3.*

$\begin{aligned}12 x + 3 y & = & 75 \left(3\right) \\ x - 3 y & = & 16 \left(2\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Eliminate the **y** terms by adding equation (3) to equation (2). Be careful to add every term. *

> *The coefficients of **y** are the same but with different signs, so add them.*

$\begin{array}{r} 12 x + 3 y = 75 \\ \underline{+ \left( x - 3 y = 16\right) } \\ 13 x = 91 \end{array}$

**[1]**

> *Solve the equation to find** x  **by dividing both sides by 13.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{91}{13} = 7\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute *$x=7$* into either of the two original equations**.*

$\left(1\right) 4 \left(7\right) + y = 25$

**[1]**

> *Solve this equation to find** y.*

$\begin{aligned}4 \left(7\right) + y & = & 25 \\ 28 + y & = & 25 \\ y & = & 25 - 28 = - 3\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute **x** = 7  and **y** = - 3 into the other equation to check that they are correct*

$\begin{aligned}\left(2\right) x - 3 y & = & 16 \\ \left(7\right) - 3 \left(- 3\right) & = & 16 \\ 7 + 9 & = & 16 \\ 16 & = & 16\end{aligned}$

$x=7,y=-3$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Solve the simultaneous equations

$2x-y=13\,x-2y=11$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Number the equations.*

> $\begin{aligned}2 x - y & = & 13 \left(1\right) \\ x - 2 y & = & 11 \left(2\right)\end{aligned}$* *

> *Make the **y** terms equal by multiplying all parts of equation (1) by 2.*

$\begin{aligned}4 x - 2 y & = & 26 \left(3\right) \\ x - 2 y & = & 11 \left(2\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Eliminate the **y** terms by subtracting equation (2) from equation (3). Be careful to subtract every term. The coefficients of **y** are the same with the same signs, so subtract them.*

$\begin{array}{r} 4 x - 2 y = 26 \\ \underline{- \left( x - 2 y = 11\right) } \\ 3 x = 15 \end{array}$

**[1]**

> *Solve the equation to find** x  **by dividing both sides by 3.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{15}{3} = 5\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute *$x=5$* into either of the two original equations**.*

$\left(1\right) 2 \left(5\right) - y = 13$

**[1]**

> *Solve this equation to find** y.*

$\begin{aligned}10 - y & = & 13 \\ - y & = & 13 - 10 = 3 \\ y & = & - 3\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute **x** = 5 and **y** = -3 into the other equation to check that they are correct*

$\begin{aligned}\left(2\right) x - 2 y & = & 11 \\ \left(5\right) - 2 \left(- 3\right) & = & 11 \\ 5 + 6 & = & 11 \\ 11 & = & 11\end{aligned}$

$x=5,y=-3$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Solve the simultaneous equations

$3x+y=-4$

$3x-4y=6$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Number the equations.*

> $3 x + y = - 4 ( 1 )$
$3 x - 4 y = 6 ( 2 )$* *

> *Eliminate the **x** terms by subtracting equation (2) from equation (1). Be careful to subtract every term. *

> *The coefficients of **x** are the same with the same signs, so subtract them.*

$\begin{array}{r} 3 x + y = - 4 \\ \underline{- \left(3 x - 4 y = 6\right)} \\ 5 y = - 10 \end{array}$

**[1]**

> *Solve the equation to find** y **by dividing both sides by 5.*

$\begin{aligned}y & = & \frac{- 10}{5} = - 2\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute *$y=-2$* into either of the two original equations**.*

$\left(1\right) 3 x + \left(- 2\right) = - 4$

**[1]**

> *Solve this equation to find** y.*

$\begin{aligned}3 x - 2 & = & - 4 \\ 3 x & = & - 4 + 2 \\ 3 x & = & - 2 \\ x & = & - \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute *$x=-\frac{2}{3}$* and *$y=-2$* into the other equation to check that they are correct.*

$\begin{aligned}\left(2\right) 3 x - 4 y & = & 6 \\ 3 \left(- \frac{2}{3}\right) - 4 \left(- 2\right) & = & 6 \\ - 2 + 8 & = & 6 \\ 6 & = & 6\end{aligned}$

$x=-\frac{2}{3},y=-2$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Solve the simultaneous equations

$\begin{aligned}4 x  +  5 y  & = &  4  \\ 2 x  –  y  & = &  9\end{aligned}$

Show clear algebraic working.
parts.solutionMd:
> *We could use the method of making the **x** terms equal (multiply second equation by 2) or by making the **y** terms equal (multiply the second equation by 5).*

> *Alternatively, as one of the equation has a single **y** term, we can rearrange it to make **y** the subject and then substitute into the other equation.*

> *Start by rearranging the second equation.*

$\begin{aligned}2 x & = & 9 + y \\ y & = & 2 x - 9\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute this rearrangement into the first equation.*

$4 x + 5 \left(2 x - 9\right) = 4$

**[1]**

> *Expand and simplify to form an equation in **x**.*

$\begin{aligned}4 x + 10 x - 45 - 4 & = & 0 \\ 14 x - 49 & = & 0\end{aligned}$

> *Solve for **x**.*

$\begin{aligned}14 x & = & 49 \\ x & = & \frac{49}{14} = 3 . 5\end{aligned}$

*Substitute this value of **x** into either of the original equations to find **y**.*

> *(In this case it will actually be easiest to use our rearranged *$y=2x-9$*.)*

$y=2\times3.5-9=-2$

**[1]**

> *Write the final answer down, making sure **x** and **y** are the correct way round!*

$x=3.5,y=-2$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Solve the simultaneous equations

$\begin{aligned}4 x  +  2 y  & = &  9 \text{   } \\ x  –  4 y  & = &  9\end{aligned}$

Show clear algebraic working.

$x=\,y=$
parts.solutionMd:
> *We could use the method of making the **x** terms equal (multiply second equation by 4) or by making the **y** terms equal (multiply the first equation by 2).*

> *Alternatively, as one of the equation has a single **x** term, we can rearrange it to make **x** the subject and then substitute into the other equation.*

> *Start by rearranging the second equation to isolate **x** by adding 4**y** to both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & 9 + 4 y \\ x & = & 4 y + 9\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute this rearrangement into the first equation.*

$4 \left(4 y + 9\right) + 2 y = 9$

**[1]**

> *Expand and simplify to form an equation in **y**.*

$\begin{aligned}16 y + 36 + 2 y - 9 & = & 0 \\ 18 y + 27 & = & 0\end{aligned}$

> *Solve for **y**.*

$\begin{aligned}18 y & = & - 27 \\ y & = & \frac{- 27}{18} = - 1 . 5\end{aligned}$

*Substitute this value of **y** into either of the original equations to find **x**.*

> *(In this case it will actually be easiest to use our rearranged *$x=4y+9$*.)*

$x=4\times-1.5+9=3$

**[1]**

> *Write the final answer down, making sure **x** and **y** are the correct way round!*

$x=3,y=-1.5$ **[1]**

> *We could use the method of making the **x** terms equal (multiply the first equation by 7) or by making the **y** terms equal (multiply the first equation by 5).*

> *Alternatively, as one of the equation has a single **x** term (and a single **y** term), we can rearrange it to make **x** (or **y**) the subject and then substitute into the other equation.*

> *Start by rearranging the first equation to isolate **x** by subtracting **y** from both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & 15 - y\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute this rearrangement into the second equation.*

$7 \left(15 - y\right) - 5 y = 3$

**[1]**

> *Expand and simplify to form an equation in **y**.*

$\begin{aligned}105 - 7 y - 5 y - 3 & = & 0 \\ - 12 y + 102 & = & 0\end{aligned}$

> *It would be nice to have a positive **y** term to make the equation easier to solve, and we can also divide through by 6.*

> * Another way of thinking of this is dividing the equation by -6.*

$2y-17=0$

> *Solve for **y**.*

$\begin{aligned}y & = & 8 . 5\end{aligned}$

*Substitute this value of **y** into either of the original equations to find **x**.*

> *(In this case it will actually be easiest to use our rearranged *$x=15-y$*.)*

$x = 15 - \left(8 . 5\right) = 6 . 5$

**[1]**

> *Write the final answer down, making sure **x** and **y** are the correct way round!*

$x=6.5,y=8.5$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Solve the simultaneous equations

$\begin{aligned}x  +  2 y  & = &  - 0 . 5 \\ 3 x  -  y  & = &  16\end{aligned}$

Show clear algebraic working.

$x=...............\,y=...............$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Number the equations.*

> $x + 2 y = - 0.5 ( 1 )$
$3 x - y = 16 ( 2 )$* *

> *Multiply equation (2) by 2 so both equations have the same number of **y**'s in them (don't worry about signs at this stage).*

$6 x - 2 y = 32 \left(3\right)$

> *Considering equations (1) and (3) we can eliminate **y** by adding these together (signs of the **y** terms are opposite so add).*

$\begin{aligned}x + 2 y & = & - 0 . 5 \\ 6 x - 2 y & = & 32 \\ 7 x & = & 31 . 5\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Solve this equation to find** x **by dividing both sides by 7.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{31 . 5}{7} = \frac{9}{2} = 4 . 5\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute *$x=4.5$* into either of the two original equations**.*

$\left(1\right) 4 . 5 + 2 y = - 0 . 5$

**[1]**

> *Solve this equation to find** y **(subtract 4.5 from both sides and then divide by 2)**.*

$\begin{aligned}2 y & = & - 5 \\ y & = & - 2 . 5 \end{aligned}$

> *Substitute *$x=4.5$* and *$y=-2.5$* into the other original equation to check that they are correct.*

$\begin{aligned}\left(2\right) 3 x - y & = & 16 \\ 3 \left(4 . 5\right) - \left(- 2 . 5\right) & = & 13 . 5 + 2 . 5 \\ & = & 16 \\ & & \end{aligned}$

$x=4.5,y=-2.5$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Solve the simultaneous equations

$\begin{aligned}3 x  +  5 y  & = &  6  \\ 7 x  –  5 y  & = &  – 11\end{aligned}$

Show clear algebraic working.

$\begin{aligned}x  & = &  . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . \\ y  & = &  . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .\end{aligned}$
parts.solutionMd:
> *Number the equations.*

> $3 x + 5 y = 6 ( 1 )$
$7 x - 5 y = - 11 ( 2 )$* *

> *Eliminate the **y** terms by adding equation (2) to equation (1) as the **y** terms have opposite signs.*

$\begin{aligned}3 x + 5 y & = & 6 \\ 7 x - 5 y & = & - 11 \\ 10 x & = & - 5\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Solve the equation to find** x **by dividing both sides by 10.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{- 5}{10} = - 0 . 5\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute *$x=-0.5$* into either of the two original equations**.*

$\left(1\right) 3 \left(- 0 . 5\right) + 5 y = 6$

> *Solve this equation to find** y.*

$\begin{aligned}- 1 . 5 + 5 y & = & 6 \\ 5 y & = & 7 . 5 \\ y & = & 1 . 5\end{aligned}$

> *Substitute *$x=-0.5$* and *$y=1.5$* into the other original equation to check that they are correct.*

$\begin{aligned}\left(2\right) 7 x - 5 y & = & 7 \left(- 0 . 5\right) - 5 \left(1 . 5\right) \\ & = & - 3 . 5 - 7 . 5 \\ & = & - 11\end{aligned}$

> *Be sure to get **x** and **y** the right way round for your final answer!*

> $x=-0.5,y=1.5$* *

**One mark for each**** [2]**

parts.problemMd:
Two straight lines intersect at point $P$.

|---|---|---|---|
parts.solutionMd:
> *The point **P** is on *$y=-1$* so takes the form *$\left(. . . , - 1\right)$* so we can immediately rule out the second and third options.*

> *Substitute *$y=-1$* into *$y=3x$* as **P **is where these two lines meet.*

$-1=3x$
