parts.problemMd:
A shaded semicircle is inside a circle as shown.

![q9-paper-1h-june-2019-aqa-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/circles-arcs-and-sectors/assets/063-q9-paper-1h-june-2019-aqa-gcse-maths.png)

The **radius **of the circle is 10 cm 
The **diameter **of the semicircle is 8 cm

How many times bigger is the unshaded area than the shaded area?
parts.solutionMd:
> *The unshaded area can be found by subtracting the area of the semi-circle from the area of the circle.*

> *Find the area of the circle, the formula for the area of a circle is *$πr^{2}$*.*

> *It's best to keep your working in terms of *$π$* to preserve the accuracy of your final answer.*

$A r e a_{\left(c i r c l e\right)} = \pi \times 10^{2} = 100 \pi$* *

**[1]**

> *Find the area of the shaded region (semicircle) using the formula *$\frac{1}{2}πr^{2}$*. The radius of the semicircle is half of the diameter of the semicircle.*

$A r e a_{\left(s e m i c i r c l e\right)} = \frac{1}{2} \pi \left(\frac{8}{2}\right)^{2} = \frac{1}{2} \pi \left(4\right)^{2} = \frac{16}{2} \pi = 8 \pi$

**[1]**

> *The area of the unshaded region = Area (circle) - Area (semicircle).*

$A r e a_{\left(c i r c l e\right)} - A r e a_{\left(s e m i c i r c l e\right)} = 100 \pi - 8 \pi = 92 \pi$

**[1]**

> *So the shaded area is 8**π **and the unshaded area is 92**π.  **Find how many times 92**π **is bigger than 8**π **by dividing 92 by 8.*

$\frac{92π}{8π}=\frac{92}{8}=11.5$

**The unshaded area is 11.5 times bigger than the shaded area ****[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Here are two watch faces, **A** and **B**.

![q1-4-6-very-hard-edexcel-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/circles-arcs-and-sectors/assets/021-q1-4-6-very-hard-edexcel-gcse-maths.png)

Both watch faces are circular with radius 2cm.

The materials used to make both watch faces have the same thickness.

**A** is made entirely of plastic. 
**B** has a 20° sector of metal and a 340° sector of plastic.

The ratio of the cost per cm<sup>2</sup> of the metal to the cost per cm<sup>2</sup> of the plastic is 3 : 2

Work out the ratio of the cost of the materials for **A** to the cost of the materials for **B**. 
Give your answer in its simplest form. 
You must show all your working.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Calculate the area of face A, using the formula for the area of a circle: *$A=πr^{2}$*, where *$r$* is the radius of the circle.*

$\begin{aligned}A & = & \pi \times 2^{2} \\ & = & 4 \pi cm^{2}\end{aligned}$

> *Find the relative cost of the materials for face A by multiplying the area by 2.*

$\begin{aligned}C_{A} & = & 2 \times 2 \pi \\ & = & 8 \pi\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Calculate the area of the metal part of face B, using the formula for the area of a sector: *$A=\frac{θ^{\circ}}{360^{\circ}}\timesπr^{2}$*, where *$θ$* is the angle of the sector.*

$\begin{aligned}A_{m e t a l} & = & \frac{20}{360} \times \pi \times 2^{2} \\ & = & \frac{2}{9} \pi cm^{2}\end{aligned}$

> *Calculate the area of the plastic part of face B by subtracting the area of the metal part from the area of the whole face.*

$\begin{aligned}A_{p l a s t i c} & = & 4 \pi - \frac{2}{9} \pi \\ & = & \frac{34}{9} \pi cm^{2}\end{aligned}$

> *Find the relative cost of the materials for face B by multiplying the plastic area by 2 and the metal area by 3 and adding together.*

$\begin{aligned}C_{B} & = & 3 \times \frac{2}{9} \pi + 2 \times \frac{34}{9} \pi \\ & = & \frac{74}{9} \pi\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Find a ratio for the cost of materials for face A to face B.*

$A:B\,8π:\frac{74}{9}π$

**[1]**

$8:\frac{74}{9}\,72:74$

$36:37$* ***[1]**

parts.solutionMd:

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}A C cos \left(30\right) & = & 24 \\ A C & = & \frac{24}{ cos \left(30\right)} \\ & = & 16 \sqrt{3} cm\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}d & = & 3 \times 2 = 6 cm\end{aligned}$

> *Calculate the length of the arc **FED**, using the formula for the circumference of a circle: *$C=2πr$*, and dividing the result by 2.*

**[1]**

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows a sector $OBC$ of a circle with centre $O$ and radius $(6+x)\mathrm{cm}$.

![q22-4ma1-2h-qp-jan21-paper2-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/circles-arcs-and-sectors/assets/007-q22-4ma1-2h-qp-jan21-paper2-igcse-maths.png)

$A$ is the point on $OB$ and $D$ is the point on $OC$ such that $OA=OD=6\mathrm{cm}$

Angle $BOC=50^{\circ}$

Given that

the perimeter of sector $OBC=2\times$the perimeter of triangle $OAD$

find the value of $x$. 
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Find the perimeter of the triangle **OAD **by first using the cosine rule, *$a^{2} = b^{2} + c^{2} - 2 b c cos \left(A\right)$*.*

> *Substitute the values of the sides (both 6 cm) and angle (50°) into the cosine rule formula.*

$\begin{aligned}A D^{2} & = & 6^{2} + 6^{2} - \left(2 \times 6 \times 6 \times cos 50\right) \\ A D & = & \sqrt{ 6^{2} + 6^{2} - \left(2 \times 6 \times 6 \times cos 50\right)} \\ & = & 5 . 071419 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Find the perimeter of triangle **OAD.*

*Perimeter of ***OAD *** = 6 + 6 + 5.071419... = 17.071419... cm**<sup> </sup>*

**[1]**

> *Find the length of the arc **BC **using the formula for length of an arc *$=\frac{θ^{\circ}}{360^{\circ}}\times2πr$*. *
*Find an expression for the length of the arc in terms of *$x$*, **by substituting *$θ=50$* and *$r=(6+x)$*.*

$B C = \frac{50}{360} \times 2 \times \pi \times \left(x + 6\right)$

**[1]**

> *Find an expression for the perimeter of the sector **OBC** in terms of *$x$*, **by adding this to 2 × the radius.*

$\begin{aligned}O B C & = & \left( \frac{50}{360} \times 2 \times \pi \times \left(x + 6\right) \right) + 2 \left(x + 6\right) \\ & = & \frac{5}{18} \left(x + 6\right) \pi + 2 \left(x + 6\right) \end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Form an equation by setting this equal to 2 times the perimeter of triangle **OAD**. *

$\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{18} \left(x + 6\right) \pi + 2 \left(x + 6\right) & = & 2 \left(17 . 071419 . . .\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify by expanding the brackets on both sides and collecting like terms.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{5 \pi}{18} x + \frac{5 \pi}{3} + 2 x + 12 & = & 34 . 14283 . . . \\ 2 . 872664 . . . x & = & 16 . 90684 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Solve the equation.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{16 . 90684 . . .}{2 . 872664 . . .} = 5 . 885422 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Round to 3 significant figures.*

$x=5.89$** cm**<sup>** **</sup>**(3 s.f.)**** [1] **
**Answers in the range 5.88 to 5.89 accepted.**

parts.problemMd:
$A,B$ and $C$ are points on a circle with centre $O$.

![q20-4ma1-2hr-qp-jan21-paper2-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/circles-arcs-and-sectors/assets/008-q20-4ma1-2hr-qp-jan21-paper2-igcse-maths.png)

Angle $ABC=75^{\circ}$

The area of the shaded segment is 200cm<sup>2</sup>

Calculate the radius of the circle. 
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

...................................................... cm
parts.solutionMd:
> *Angle **AOC **is made by drawing lines from the points **A** and **C **on the circle which meet at the centre (**O**).*

*The circle theorem states that the angle at the centre is double the angle at the circumference.* 
*Therefore angle **AOC **is double angle **ABC**.*

![ed-igcse-arcs-and-sectors-vh-q5-diagram-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/circles-arcs-and-sectors/assets/009-ed-igcse-arcs-and-sectors-vh-q5-diagram-1.png)

$\mathrm{Angle}AOC=2\times75^{\circ}=150^{\circ}$

**[1]**

> *Form an expression for the area of the sector **AOC **using the formula for area of a sector *$=\frac{θ}{360^{\circ}}\timesπr^{2}$* and substituting the values into the formula, letting *$θ=150$* and *$r=r$*.*

$\mathrm{Area}_{\mathrm{sector}}=\frac{150}{360}\timesπ\timesr^{2}=\frac{5}{12}πr^{2}$

**[1]**

> *Form an expression for the area of the triangle **AOC **using the formula for area of a triangle *$=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}θ$* and substituting the values into the formula, letting *$θ=150$* and *$r=r$*.*

$\mathrm{Area}_{\mathrm{triangle}}=\frac{1}{2}\timesr\timesr\times\mathrm{sin}150=\frac{1}{4}r^{2}$

**[1]**

> *Form an expression for the area of the shaded region by subtracting the area of the triangle from the area of sector **AOC.*

$\mathrm{Area}_{\mathrm{shaded}}=\frac{5}{12}πr^{2}-\frac{1}{4}r^{2}$

> *Form an equation by setting the expression for the area of the shaded region equal to 200 cm*<sup>*2*</sup>*.*

$\frac{5}{12}πr^{2}-\frac{1}{4}r^{2}=200$

**[1]**

> *Factorise out **r*<sup>*2*</sup>*.*

$r^{2} \left(\frac{5}{12} \pi - \frac{1}{4}\right) = 200$

> *Isolate **r*<sup>*2*</sup>*.*

$r^{2} = \frac{200}{\left(\frac{5}{12} \pi - \frac{1}{4}\right) }$

> *Solve to find **r **by taking the square root of both sides.*

$r = \sqrt{\frac{200}{\left(\frac{5}{12} \pi - \frac{1}{4}\right) }} = 13 . 74256 . . .$

> *Round to 3 significant figures.*

**radius = 13.7 cm**<sup>** **</sup>**(3 s.f.)**** [1] **
**Answers in the range 13.7 to 13.8 accepted**

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows two circles such that the region $R$, shown shaded in the diagram, is the region common to both circles.

![q25-4ma1-1h-qp-june21-paper1-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/circles-arcs-and-sectors/assets/013-q25-4ma1-1h-qp-june21-paper1-igcse-maths.png)

One of the circles has centre $O$ and radius 5cm. 
The other circle has centre $P$ and radius 4 cm. 
Angle $AOB=50^{\circ}$

Calculate the area of region $R$. 
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

...................................................... cm<sup>2</sup>
parts.solutionMd:
> *The area of the region **R **is the area of the larger segment from circle centre **O** added to the area of the smaller segment from circle centre **P**. *

![ed-igcse-arcs-and-sectors-vh-q4-diagram-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/circles-arcs-and-sectors/assets/014-ed-igcse-arcs-and-sectors-vh-q4-diagram-1.png)

> *To find the area of the segment in circle centre **O, **subtract the area of triangle **AOB **from the area of sector **AOB.*

> *Find the area of triangle **AOB** using the area of a triangle formula, *$A=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where *$a$* and *$b$* are the two known sides and *$C$* is the included angle. **OA **and **OB **are both radii so are both equal to 5 cm.*

$A r e a_{t r i a n g l e A O B} = \frac{1}{2} \times \left(5\right) \times \left(5\right) \times sin \left(50\right) = \frac{25}{2} sin 50$

> *It is best to leave working as exact values as you work through the problem, but if you choose to round make sure you use at least 4 significant figures throughout. *

> *Find the area of the sector **AOB **using the formula for area of a sector *$=\frac{θ}{360^{\circ}}\timesπr^{2}$*.*

> *Substitute the given values into the formula, letting *$θ=50$* and *$r=5$*.*

$\frac{50}{360}\timesπ\times5^{2}=\frac{125}{36}π$

**[1]**

> *Find the area of the segment by subtracting the area of triangle **AOB **from the area of sector **AOB.*

*Area segment (circle ***O***) =*$\frac{125}{36}π-\frac{25}{2}\mathrm{sin}50$

> *To find the area of the segment in circle centre **P, **we first need to find angle **APB.*

> *Triangles **AOB **and **APB **are both isosceles triangles so the line **OP **is a line of symmetry. The sine rule can be used with triangle **AOP **to find the value of angle **APO **which can then be doubled to find angle **APB.*

![ed-igcse-arcs-and-sectors-vh-q4-diagram-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/circles-arcs-and-sectors/assets/015-ed-igcse-arcs-and-sectors-vh-q4-diagram-2.png)

> *Use the sine rule with the angles on the numerators, *$\frac{\mathrm{sin}A}{a}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}B}{b}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}C}{c}$*.*

$\frac{sin \left(A P O\right)}{5} = \frac{sin \left(25\right)}{4}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 5 and use the inverse sin to find the angle **APO**.*

$\text{sin} A P O = 5 \times \frac{ \text{sin} 25}{4} = 0.528272...$
$\text{angle} A P O = \text{sin} ^{ - } 1 ( 0.528272... ) = 31.88883...$

**[1]**

> *Angle **APB **= 2 × angle **APO**.*

$A P B = 2 \left(31 . 88883 . . .\right) = 63 . 77766 . . .$

> *Find the area of triangle **APB** using the area of a triangle formula, *$A=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*.*

$A r e a_{t r i a n g l e A P B} = \frac{1}{2} \times \left(4\right) \times \left(4\right) \times sin \left(63 . 77766 . . .\right) = 7 . 176689 . . .$

> *Find the area of the sector **APB **using the formula for area of a sector *$=\frac{θ}{360^{\circ}}\timesπr^{2}$*.*

$\frac{63.77766...}{360}\timesπ\times4^{2}=8.905041...$

**[1]**

> *Find the area of the segment by subtracting the area of triangle **APB **from the area of sector **APB.*

*Area segment (circle ***P***) = *$8.905041...-7.176689...=1.728352...$

> *Find the area of the shaded section by adding the area of the two segments together.*

*Area shaded = *$\left(\frac{125}{36} \pi - \frac{25}{2} sin 50\right) + 1 . 728352 . . . = 3 . 061104 . . .$

**[1]**

> *Round the final answer to 3 significant figures. *

**Area = 3.06 cm**<sup>**2**</sup>** ****[1] **
**Answers in the range 3 to 3.1 accepted**

parts.problemMd:

![q26-4ma1-2h-qp-jan20-paper2-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/circles-arcs-and-sectors/assets/025-q26-4ma1-2h-qp-jan20-paper2-igcse-maths.png)

The sector can form the curved surface of a cone by joining $OA$to $OB$ .

![q26-14ma1-2h-qp-jan20-paper2-igcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/circles-arcs-and-sectors/assets/026-q26-14ma1-2h-qp-jan20-paper2-igcse-maths.png)

The height of the cone is $25\mathrm{cm}$. 
The volume of the cone is $1600\mathrm{cm}^{3}$

Work out the value of $x.$ 
Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.

$x=$.......................
parts.solutionMd:
> *The formula for the volume of a cone, *$V=\frac{1}{3}πr^{2}h$*, is given at the beginning of the paper. *
*Use the formula with the given volume of the cone to find the value of the radius of the base circle. *
*Using the known volume of 1600 cm*<sup>*3*</sup>* we can write the following equation.*

$\frac{1}{3}\timesπ\timesr^{2}\times25=1600$

**[1]**

> *Divide both sides by 25 and *$\frac{1}{3}π$*.*

$\frac{1}{3}πr^{2}=\frac{1600}{25}=64$

$r^{2}=\frac{64}{\frac{π}{3}}=\frac{192}{π}=61.11549...$

> *Square root both sides.*

$r=\sqrt{61.11549...}=7.817640...$

**[1]**

> *The formula for the curved surface area of a cone, *$πrl$* , is given at the beginning of the paper.*

> *Use Pythagoras' Theorem to find the value of *$l$*, the slant height of the cone. *

![ed-igcse-arcs-and-sectors-vh-q6-diagram-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/circles-arcs-and-sectors/assets/027-ed-igcse-arcs-and-sectors-vh-q6-diagram-1.png)

> *It is a right angled triangle so you can use Pythagoras' Theorem: *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$*, where **c** is the length of the hypotenuse (the slant height) and **a** and **b **are the height and the radius. *

$\begin{aligned}l^{2} & = & 7 . 81764 . . .^{2} + 25^{2} \\ l & = & \sqrt{7 . 81764 . . .^{2} + 25^{2}} \\ & = & 26 . 193806 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Substitute the values of *$l$* and *$r$* into the formula for the curved surface area of a cone.*

$\begin{aligned}C S A & = & \pi r l = \pi \left(7 . 817640 . . .\right) \left(26 . 193806 . . .\right) = 643 . 313706 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *The area of the sector is equal to the curved surface area of the cone. Use the formula for area of a sector *$\frac{θ}{360^{\circ}}\timesπr^{2}$*, where the radius of the sector is equal to the slant height of the cone, to find the value of the angle, *$x$*.*

$\frac{x}{360} \times \pi \times \begin{aligned} & & 26\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & .\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & 193806\end{aligned} . . .^{2} = \begin{aligned} & & 643\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & .\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & 313706\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & .\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & .\end{aligned} \begin{aligned} & & .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange and solve to find *$x$*.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{x}{360} & = & \frac{643 . 313706 . . .}{ 26 . 193806 . . .^{2} \times \pi } \\ \frac{x}{360} & = & 0 . 298452 . . . \\ x & = & 0 . 298452 . . . \times 360 = 107 . 4430 . . .\end{aligned}$

$x=107^{\circ}$ **[1]** 
**Rounded to 3 significant figures** **107 - 108 allowed**

parts.problemMd:

$OPQ$ is a sector of a circle, centre $O$
 $OAB$ is a sector of a circle, centre $O$

$A\mathrm{is} \mathrm{the} \mathrm{point} \mathrm{on}OP\mathrm{such} \mathrm{that}OA:AP=3:2\,B\mathrm{is} \mathrm{the} \mathrm{point} \mathrm{on}OQ\mathrm{such} \mathrm{that}OB:BQ=3:2$ 
Angle $POQ=45^{\circ}$

Work out the perimeter of the shaded region.

parts.solutionMd:
> *First convert the ratios for each radius into fractions of the length of **OP** and **OQ.*

**OA ***= *$\frac{3}{3+2}=\frac{3}{5}$* of ***OP***.*

parts.solutionMd:
> *The formula for the circumference of a circle is *$2πr=\mathrm{πd}$*. *
*Find an expression for the circumference of the circle in terms of *$r.$

$C=2πr$* *

**[1]**

> *The perimeter of the sector is equal to the arc length of the sector plus the two straight edges (both radii).*

*The arc length of a sector (the length of the curved side) with radius *$r$* and angle *$θ$*° is *$\frac{θ}{360}\times2πr$*.* 
*Find an expression for the arc length of the sector by substituting *$θ=x$* and *$r=r$* into the formula.*

$\mathrm{Arc} \mathrm{length}=\frac{x}{360}\times2π\timesr=\frac{2πrx}{360}$

**[1]**

> *Find an expression for the perimeter of the sector by adding *$2r$* for the two straight edges.*

$\mathrm{Perimeter}=\frac{2πrx}{360}+2r$

> *Form an equation by setting the expressions for the circumference of the circle equal to the perimeter of the sector.*

$2πr=\frac{2πrx}{360}+2r$

**[1]**

> *Begin to simplify by dividing both sides by 2**r.*

$\begin{aligned}\cancel{2} \pi \cancel{r} & = & \frac{\cancel{2} \pi \cancel{r} x}{360} + \cancel{2 r} \\ \pi & = & \frac{\pi x}{360} + 1\end{aligned}$

> *Rearrange to make **x **the subject. *

$\begin{aligned}\pi - 1 & = & \frac{\pi x}{360} \\ 360 \left(\pi - 1\right) & = & \pi x \end{aligned}$

**71 laps*** ***[1]**

The area of sector OAB is 6$π$cm<sup>2</sup>. 
Show that AX = 3 $\sqrt{3}$ cm.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Use the formula for the area of the sector set equal to 6**π **cm*<sup>*2 *</sup>*and solve to find the angle AOB. *

> *The formula for the area of a sector is *$\frac{θ}{360}\timesπr^{2}$* , where **θ** is the angle at the centre and **r** is the radius.*

> *Apply this formula to the given sector with **r **= 6 cm and area = 6**π **cm.*

$6π=\frac{θ}{360}\timesπ\times6^{2}$

**Correct expression**** [1] **
**Correct equation**** [1]**

> *Simplify the right-hand side.*

$\begin{aligned}6 \pi & = & \frac{\theta}{360} \times 36 \times \pi \\ & = & \frac{\theta}{10} \times \pi \end{aligned}$

> *Cancel out **π **from both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}6 & = & \frac{\theta}{10} \end{aligned}$

> *Multiply both sides by 10*

$θ=6\times10=60^{\circ}$

**[1]**

> *Triangle AOX is a right-angled triangle with one know angle and one known side, so SOHCAHTOA can be used to find the missing side.  You know the length of the hypotenuse (**H**) and you want the length of the side that is opposite (**O**) the angle. Therefore you can use the sine ratio: *$\mathrm{sin}θ=\frac{O}{H}$*.*

$sin \left(60\right) = \frac{A X}{6}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 6 to get **AX **by itself.*

$\begin{aligned}A X & = & 6 \times sin \left(60\right)\end{aligned}$

> *The exact value of sin(60) is *$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$*, substitute this in and simplify.*

$\begin{aligned}A X & = & 6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}\mathbf{\mathit{A}} \mathbf{\mathit{X}} & = & 6 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 3 \sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$ **[1] **

parts.solutionMd:
> *QR** and **BC** are corresponding lengths in similar shapes so find **k, **the scale factor, using**  *$\begin{aligned}k & = & \frac{second corresponding length}{first corresponding length}\end{aligned}$

> *Method 1*

> *BC** is smaller than **QR. **To go from the big shape to the small shape, put the small length on top in the fraction so that **k** will be smaller than 1*

$\begin{aligned}k & = & \frac{A B}{P Q} = \frac{4}{12} = \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}B C & = & k Q R = \frac{1}{3} \times 16 . 5\end{aligned}$

> *Method 2 *
*Finding **k** using *$\begin{aligned}k & = & \frac{second corresponding length}{first corresponding length} ,\end{aligned}$* if you put the larger length on top in the fraction then;*

$\begin{aligned}k & = & \frac{P Q}{A B} = \frac{12}{4} = 3\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Notice that **k** > 1 so multiplying by **k** will make the length bigger- but in going from **QR **to **BC, **we want to go from a longer length to a smaller length. So divide by **k** instead*

$\begin{aligned}B C & = & Q R \div k \\ & = & 16 . 5 \div 3\end{aligned}$

The real height of tower $A$ is $187m$. 
The real height of tower $B$ is $147m$.

Ahmed makes a scale model of both towers.

The height of tower $A$ on the scale model is $90\mathrm{cm}$.

Work out the height of tower $B$ on the scale model. 
Give your answer correct to the nearest centimetre.
parts.solutionMd:
> *The height of model **A** and the height of model **B** are corresponding lengths in similar shapes so find **k, **the scale factor, using**  *$\begin{aligned}k & = & \frac{second corresponding length}{first corresponding length}\end{aligned}$

> *Method 1*

> *The height of model **B** is smaller than the height of model **A**. **To go from the big shape to the small shape, put the small length on top in the fraction so that **k** will be smaller than 1*

$\begin{aligned}k & = & \frac{height \mathbf{B}}{height \mathbf{A}} = \frac{147}{187}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Find the height of model **B** by multiplying the height of model **A** by **k **(notice that **k** < 1 so multiplying by **k** will make the length smaller)*

$\begin{aligned}height \mathbf{B} & = & k \left[height \mathbf{A}\right] = \frac{147}{187} \times 90\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned} & = & 70 . 7486631 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *This answer is already in centimetres but give the final answer to the nearest centimetre as requested in the question*

**71 cm**** ****[1]**

> *Method 2*

> *Finding **k **using**  *$\begin{aligned}k & = & \frac{second corresponding length}{first corresponding length}\end{aligned}$*, if you put the larger length on top of the fraction then;*

$\begin{aligned}k & = & \frac{height \mathbf{A}}{height \mathbf{B}} = \frac{187}{147} \end{aligned}$

> *Notice that **k** > 1 so multiplying by **k** will make the length bigger- but in going from the height of model **A** to the height of model of **B**, we want to go from a longer length to a smaller length. So divide by **k **instead*

$\begin{aligned}height \mathbf{B} & = & height \mathbf{A} \div k = 90 \div \frac{187}{147}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned} & = & 70 . 7486631 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *This answer is already in centimetres but give the final answer to the nearest centimetre as requested in the question*

**71 cm ****[1]**

Prove that triangles PQS and QRS are similar.
parts.solutionMd:
> *Calculate the length of side QS on triangle QRS. *
*Use Pythagoras' theorem, *$c^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}$*, where *$a$* and *$b$* are the lengths of the two shorter sides and *$c$* is the length of the hypotenuse.*

$\begin{aligned}Q S^{2} & = & 4^{2} + 8^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$QS=\sqrt{4^{2}+8^{2}}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}Q S & = & \sqrt{80} \\ Q S & = & \sqrt{16 \times 5} \\ Q S & = & 4 \sqrt{5}\end{aligned}$

> *Now that you know the length QS you can use Pythagoras' theorem again to calculate the length QP on triangle PQS.*

$\begin{aligned}10^{2} & = & Q P^{2} + \left(4 \sqrt{5}\right)^{2} \\ 10^{2} - \left(4 \sqrt{5}\right)^{2} & = & Q P^{2} \\ \sqrt{10^{2} - \left(4 \sqrt{5}\right)^{2}} & = & Q P \\ \sqrt{100 - 80} & = & Q P \\ \sqrt{20} & = & Q P \\ 2 \sqrt{5} & = & Q P\end{aligned}$

> *Compare the ratios of the lengths of two pairs of corresponding sides.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{Q R}{Q P} & = & \frac{R S}{Q S} \\ \frac{4}{2 \sqrt{5}} & = & \frac{8}{4 \sqrt{5}}\end{aligned}$

> *Cancel common factors in each fraction.*

$\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}$

**[1]**

> *These two pairs of corresponding sides have the same ratio, compare this ratio to the third pair of corresponding sides.*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{Q R}{Q P} & = & \frac{Q S}{P S} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & = & \frac{4 \sqrt{5}}{10}\end{aligned}$

> *Simplify the fraction on the right hand side.*

$\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}$

> *Rationalise the denominator of the first fraction by multiplying by *$\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}}$*.*

$\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{5}\sqrt{5}}=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}$

> *Simplify.*

$\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}=\frac{2\sqrt{5}}{5}$

**[1]**

**Triangles QRS and PQS are similar because they have three pairs of corresponding sides with the same ratio ****[1]**

$PQRST$ is a regular pentagon. 
$R,U$ and $T$ are points on a circle, centre $O$. 
$QR$ and $PT$ are tangents to the circle. 
$RSU$ is a straight line.

Prove that $ST=UT$.
parts.solutionMd:
> *To prove that **ST  **is equal to** UT ** you will need to **prove **that the triangle **STU **is **isosceles**. This can be done by finding the angles. *

> *PQRST **is a regular pentagon, so the angle **TSU** is the exterior angle of a regular pentagon. Exterior angles in any polygon add up to 360°. A regular pentagon has 5 equal exterior angles.*

> * *`T S with hat on top U space equals 360 over 5 equals space 72 degree`

**[1]**

> *To find the size of angle **SUT**, you will need to consider circle theorems.*

> *Begin by joining the point **O** to the points **T** and **R,** marking all the radiuses of the circle as equal lengths on the diagram.*

> *TP** and **TR **are also tangents to the circle, so by the circle theorem 'A tangent always meets a radius at 90°', angles **ORQ **and **OTP **are both 90°. *

`O R with hat on top Q space equals space O T with hat on top P space equals 90 degree`* **(angle between tangent and radius)*

**[1]**

> *Mark these onto the diagram.*

![QLY1pOQ2_4-8-edexcel-gcse-vh-q3-diagram-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/congruence-similarity-and-geometrical-proof/assets/011-qly1poq2-4-8-edexcel-gcse-vh-q3-diagram-2.png)

> *The sum of the interior angles in any polygon can be found using the formula 180°(n - 2). A regular pentagon has 5 equal interior angles, therefore these can be found using the formula *$\frac{180 \left(5 - 2\right)}{5}$*.*

> * *$T \hat{P} Q = P \hat{Q} R = \frac{3 \left(180\right)}{5} = 108 \circ$

> *Add these angles to the diagram.*

![4-8-edexcel-gcse-vh-q3-diagram-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/congruence-similarity-and-geometrical-proof/assets/012-4-8-edexcel-gcse-vh-q3-diagram-3.png)

> *PQROT  **is a pentagon, so the angle **ROT**  can be found by subtracting the other four angles from the sun of the angles in a pentagon.*

> *The sum of the interior angles in any polygon can be found using the formula 180°(n - 2).*

$R \hat{O} T + O \hat{T} P + T \hat{P} Q + P \hat{Q} R + Q \hat{R} O = 180 \left(5 - 2\right) \circ = 540 \circ$

> *Substitute in the angles you know to find angle **ROT**.*

$\begin{aligned}R \hat{O} T + 90 \circ + 90 \circ + 108 \circ + 108 \circ & = & 540 \circ \\ R \hat{O} T + 396 \circ & = & 540 \circ \\ R \hat{O} T & = & 144 \circ\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *By the circle theorem, the angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference, angle **ROT **is twice angle **RUT.*

$R \hat{O} T = 2 \left(R \hat{U} T\right) = 2 \left(S \hat{U} T\right)$

$S \hat{U} T = \frac{R \hat{O} T}{2} = \frac{144}{2} = 72 \circ$

**[1]**

> *This proves that angle **TSU **is equal to angle **SUT **and so triangle **STU **is isosceles.*

**Therefore ****ST ****= ****UT **
**All reasons given clearly [1]**

![cie-igcse-2018-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q10bii](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/congruence-similarity-and-geometrical-proof/assets/007-cie-igcse-2018-oct-nov-p4-tz2-q10bii.png)

The volume of the smaller cone is half the volume of the original cone.

The smaller cone is melted down to make two different spheres.

The ratio of the radii of these two spheres is 1 : 2.

Calculate the radius of the smaller sphere.

[The volume, $V$, of a sphere with radius $r$ is  $V=\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}$.]

.......................................... cm
parts.solutionMd:
> *Find the volume of the smaller cone by halving the volume of the bigger cone in part (b)(i) *

$\frac{1}{2}\times3770=1885$* cm**<sup>3</sup>*

**[1]**

*Method 1* 
*The ratio of radii (lengths) is 1 : 2 so the ratio of volumes is 1*<sup>*3*</sup>* : 2*<sup>*3*</sup> *Split this volume up into the ratio 1 : 8 (by finding *$\frac{1}{9}$* of it and *$\frac{8}{9}$* of it*

> $\frac{1}{9}\times1885:\frac{8}{9}\times1885\,$* *

*The volume of the smaller sphere is *$\frac{1}{9}\times1885$ 
*Form an equation in *$r$* by setting the sphere volume formula equal to *$\frac{1}{9}\times1885$ * *

$\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}=\frac{1}{9}\times1885$

**[2]**

> *Get *$r^{3}$* on its own (by dividing both sides by *$\frac{4}{3}π$

> $r^{3}=\frac{\frac{1}{9}\times1885}{\frac{4}{3}π}\,$* *

> *Find *$r$* (by cube-rooting both sides*

$r = \sqrt[3]{\frac{\frac{1}{9} \times 1885}{\frac{4}{3} \pi}} \\$


**3.68 cm*** ***[1]**

*Method 2* 
*The ratio of radii is 1: 2 so write the smaller sphere radius as *$r$* and the bigger sphere radius as *$2r$ 
*Form an equation in *$r$* (the sum of the volumes of the two spheres equals *$1885$*)* * *

$\frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3} + \frac{4}{3} \pi \left(2 r\right)^{3} = 1885$

**[1]**

*Collect like terms, using *$\left(2 r\right)^{3} = 8 r^{3}$ * *

$\frac{4}{3}πr^{3}+\frac{4}{3}π\times8r^{3}=1885\,\frac{36}{3}πr^{3}=1885\,12πr^{3}=1885$ * *

*Find *$r$* (by dividing both sides by *$12π$* then cube-rooting)*

$r = \sqrt[3]{\frac{1885}{12 \pi}}$

**[1]** 
**3.68 cm ****[1]**

> *Find the diagonal length **DB**. **DCB** is a right angled triangle so you can use Pythagoras' Theorem: *$a^{2}+b^{2}=c^{2}$*, where **c** is the length of the hypotenuse and **a** and **b **are the lengths of the other two sides.*

 $AB$ = 5 m 
$BC$ = 3 m

Work out the total length of the four metal bars of the frame.

parts.solutionMd:
> *Method 1*

> *You know two lengths of the right angled triangle **ABC** so you can use Pythagoras' theorem to find the length **AC**.*

![4-10-edexcel-gcse-vhq4-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/right-angled-triangles---pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/025-4-10-edexcel-gcse-vhq4-1.png)

$\begin{aligned}A B^{2} + B C^{2} & = & A C^{2} \\ 5^{2} + 3^{2} & = & z^{2} \\ 34 & = & z^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Take the positive square root of both sides. Leave as an exact value.*

$\begin{aligned}z & = & \sqrt{34}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *You now know the lengths of all three sides so you can find any angle. To find **BAC, **you should use the lengths given in the question (the opposite and adjacent sides). Use the tan ratio.*

$tan \left(y\right) = \frac{3}{5}$

**[1]**

> *Find the angle by using the inverse tan function.*

$\begin{aligned}y & = & tan^{- 1} \left(\frac{3}{5}\right) \\ & = & 30 . 963756 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *You now know an angle and the length of the hypotenuse in the triangle **ABD**. You want to find the length of the side that is opposite the angle so use the sine ratio. Use the answer button or your calculator's memory to use the exact value for the angle **BAC**.*

![4-10-edexcel-gcse-vhq4-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/right-angled-triangles---pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/026-4-10-edexcel-gcse-vhq4-2.png)

$\begin{aligned}sin \left(30 . 963756 . . .\right) & = & \frac{x}{5}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 5.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & 5 \times sin \left(30 . 963756 . . .\right) \\ & = & 2 . 572478 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Add together the four lengths. Use the answer button for the length of **BD**.*

$5+3+\sqrt{34}+2.572478...=16.403430...$

> *Round to 3 significant figures. Remember to include the units for the length.*

$\mathrm{Total} \mathrm{length}=16.4m(3\mathrm{sf})$ **[1]**

> *Method 2*

> *You know two lengths of the right angled triangle **ABC** so you can use Pythagoras' theorem to find the length **AC**.*

![4-10-edexcel-gcse-vhq4-3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/right-angled-triangles---pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/027-4-10-edexcel-gcse-vhq4-3.png)

$\begin{aligned}A B^{2} + B C^{2} & = & A C^{2} \\ 5^{2} + 3^{2} & = & z^{2} \\ 34 & = & z^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Take the positive square root of both sides. Leave as an exact value.*

$\begin{aligned}z & = & \sqrt{34}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Both triangles **ABC** and **ABD** are right angled and share an angle at the corner **A**. Therefore they have the same three angles so they are similar triangles. The scale factor between the lengths in **ABC **and the corresponding lengths are equal. **AC** corresponds to **AB **(they are both the hypotenuse of their triangles)** **and **BC **corresponds to **BD** (they are both opposite the angle at **A**).*

$\begin{aligned}r^{2} & = & \frac{49}{\pi} \\ r & = & \sqrt{\frac{49}{\pi}}\end{aligned}$

> *You can form a right angled triangle using one side of the square and two radii. The length of the square is the hypotenuse of the triangle, you can use Pythagoras' theorem.*

$\begin{aligned}r^{2} + r^{2} & = & x^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}\left(\sqrt{\frac{49}{\pi}}\right)^{2} + \left(\sqrt{\frac{49}{\pi}}\right)^{2} & = & x^{2} \\ \frac{49}{\pi} + \frac{49}{\pi} & = & x^{2} \\ \frac{98}{\pi} & = & x^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Take the positive square root of both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \sqrt{\frac{98}{\pi}} \\ & = & 5 . 585191 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Round to 3 significant figures.*

$x=5.59(3\mathrm{sf})$* ***[1]**

parts.solutionMd:
> *To find the length of **AFEDC**, find the length of the hypotenuse of the right angled triangle, subtract the diameter of the semicircle and then add the arc length of the semicircle. *

> *Find the hypotenuse, *$AC$*, of the right-angled triangle **ABC** using SOHCAHTOA.*

> *You want the length of the hypotenuse and you know the length of the side that is adjacent to the angle. Therefore you can use the cosine ratio: *$cosθ=\frac{O}{H}$*.*

$cos \left(30\right) = \frac{24}{A C}$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange to get **AC** by itself.*

$\begin{aligned}A C cos \left(30\right) & = & 24 \\ A C & = & \frac{24}{ cos \left(30\right)} \\ & = & 16 \sqrt{3} cm\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}d & = & 3 \times 2 = 6 cm\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}Arc length & = & \frac{2 \times \pi \times 3}{2} = 3 \pi cm\end{aligned}$

parts.problemMd:
The diagram shows the side view of a step ladder with a horizontal strut of length 48 cm.

The strut is one third of the way up the ladder.

The symmetrical cross section of the ladder shows two similar triangles.

![q23-paper-3h-nov-2018-aqa-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/right-angled-triangles---pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/032-q23-paper-3h-nov-2018-aqa-gcse-maths.png)

Work out the vertical height, $h$ cm, of the ladder.

...........................cm
parts.solutionMd:
> *We have two similar triangles; a small triangle formed by the horizontal strut and the portion of step ladder above it, and a large triangle formed by the whole step ladder with the ground.*

> *We can label the height and the slant height of the small triangle as **H **and **L** respectively. On the diagram below, **h** is divided in the ratio 2 : 1 (because "the strut is one third of the way up the ladder");*

![gcse-aqa-tq-congruence-similarity-proof-h-5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/right-angled-triangles---pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/033-gcse-aqa-tq-congruence-similarity-proof-h-5.png)

> *If **H** is the vertical height of the small triangle formed by the horizontal strut and the ladder above it, then **H** : **h** is in the ratio 2 : 3, or  *$H=\frac{2}{3}h$*.*

> *Therefore the scale factor, **k**, between the big triangle and the small triangle is *

$k=\frac{2}{3}$

> *From this we can calculate **L**, the slant height of the small triangle.*

$L=141\times\frac{2}{3}=94\mathrm{cm}$

**[1]**

> *We can form a right-angle triangle in the small triangle, where the base is half of the 48 cm strut length:*

![gcse-aqa-tq-congruence-similarity-proof-h-5-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/right-angled-triangles---pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/034-gcse-aqa-tq-congruence-similarity-proof-h-5-2.png)

**connecting 94 and 24 in a right-angle triangle**** [1]**

> *We can find **H** using Pythagoras' Theorem*

$\begin{aligned}H & = & \sqrt{94^{2} - 24^{2}} \\ & = & 90 . 88455214 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *It is best to store this value in your calculator- but if you round it, round to at least 4 significant figures to preserve accuracy,*

> *We can connect this value for **H** with **h** using the scale factor.*

$\begin{aligned}90 . 88455214 . . . & = & \frac{2}{3} h\end{aligned}$

> *Divide both sides by *$\frac{2}{3}$* to find **h**.*

$\begin{aligned}h & = & 90 . 88455214 . . . \div \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned} & = & 136 . 3268132 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *As no level of accuracy is specified in the question, round your answer to a sensible level of accuracy- as a general rule, at least 3 significant figures but here we will use 1 decimal place.*

**Answer = 136.3 cm (1 d.p.)**** ****[1]**

parts.problemMd:
The point A is shown on the unit grid below. 
The point B is $2\sqrt{5}$ units from A and lies on the intersection of two grid lines.

Mark **one **possible position for B.

![q12b-paper4-spec2015-ocr-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/right-angled-triangles---pythagoras-and-trigonometry/assets/029-q12b-paper4-spec2015-ocr-gcse-maths.png)
parts.solutionMd:
> *If both point A and point B both lie on gridlines, then they must form a right-angled triangle where the lengths of the two shorter sides are both integer values and the length of the hypotenuse is the direct distance between A and B.*

> *Substitute the given direct distance between A and B into Pythagoras' theorem, *$c^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}$*, where *$a$* and *$b$* are the lengths of the two shorter sides and *$c$* is the length of the hypotenuse.*

$\left(2 \sqrt{5}\right)^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}$

> *Simplify, using your answer of *$\sqrt{20}=2\sqrt{5}$* from part (a).*

$\begin{aligned}\left(\sqrt{20}\right)^{2} & = & a^{2} + b^{2} \\ 20 & = & a^{2} + b^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *If a and b must be integer values, then a*<sup>*2*</sup>* and b*<sup>*2*</sup>* must be square numbers that are also integers. List all of the square numbers below 20.*

$1,4,9,16$

> *Identify a pair of square numbers that sum to 20, these are a*<sup>*2*</sup>* and b*<sup>*2*</sup>*.*

$a^{2}=4\,b^{2}=16$

**[1]**

> *Take the square root of both to find the values of a and b.*

$a=2\,b=4$

> *This means that B could be located in one of two positions, it could be:*

> *   - 2 squares to the right and 4 squares up OR*

> *   - 4 squares to the right and 2 squares up*

parts.problemMd:

![q1-medium-4-11-sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangge-edexcel-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/076-q1-medium-4-11-sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-tria.png)

Work out the area of triangle $ABC$. 
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solutionMd:
> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **C**. Substitute **a** = 7, **b** = 6 and **C** = 60 into the formula.*

$\begin{aligned}Area & = & \frac{1}{2} \times 7 \times 6 \times sin \left(60\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Type into your calculator.*

$\begin{aligned}Area & = & \frac{21 \sqrt{3}}{2} \\ & = & 18 . 186533 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Round to 3 significant figures. Remember to include square units for the area.*

$\mathrm{Area}=18.2\mathrm{cm}^{2}(3\mathrm{sf})$ **[1]**

parts.problemMd:
Work out the length of the side $AB$. 
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solutionMd:
> *You know the lengths of two sides and the angle between them and you want to find the length of the third side. Therefore you need to use the cosine rule.*

> *The formula for the cosine rule is *$a^{2}=b^{2}+c^{2}-2bc\mathrm{cos}A$*, where **b** and **c** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **A** and **a** is the length of the side opposite **A**. *
*Substitute **a** = **AB**, **b** = 6, **c** = 7 and **A** = 60 into the formula.*

$A B^{2} = 6^{2} + 7^{2} - 2 \left(6\right) \left(7\right) cos \left(60\right)$

**[1]**

> *Type the expression into your calculator altogether as one line. If you do it separately you need to remember the order of operations (multiplication before addition).*

$AB^{2}=43$

**[1]**

> *Take the positive square root of both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}A B & = & \sqrt{43} \\ & = & 6 . 557438 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Round to 3 significant figures. Remember to include units for the length.*

$AB=6.56\mathrm{cm}(3\mathrm{sf})$* ***[1]**

![q17-paper-1h-june-2018-aqa-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/069-q17-paper-1h-june-2018-aqa-gcse-maths.png)

Circle the correct equation.

| $\frac{\mathrm{sin}x}{42}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}15^{\circ}}{104}$ | $\frac{x}{\mathrm{sin}42^{\circ}}=\frac{15}{\mathrm{sin}104^{\circ}}$ |
|---|---|
| $\frac{\mathrm{sin}x}{34}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}15^{\circ}}{104}$ | $\frac{x}{\mathrm{sin}42^{\circ}}=\frac{15}{\mathrm{sin}34^{\circ}}$ |
parts.solutionMd:
> *The sine rule can be written as either *$\frac{a}{\mathrm{sin}A}=\frac{b}{\mathrm{sin}B}$* or *$\frac{\mathrm{sin}A}{a}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}B}{b}$*, where **a **and **b** are lengths of two sides of the triangle and **A** and **B **are the angles opposite the sides respectively.*

> *x** cm is opposite 42° and 15 cm is opposite 104°.*

$\frac{x}{\mathrm{sin}42}=\frac{15}{\mathrm{sin}104}\mathrm{or}\frac{\mathrm{sin}42}{x}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}104}{15}$

$\frac{x}{sin42^{\circ}}=\frac{15}{sin104^{\circ}}$** [1]**

> $\frac{\mathrm{sin}x}{42}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}15}{104}\mathrm{and}\frac{\mathrm{sin}x}{34}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}15}{104}$* can be eliminated as they both contain terms where a length is after the sin rather than an angle.*

> $\frac{x}{\mathrm{sin}42}=\frac{15}{\mathrm{sin}34}$* can be eliminated as the length opposite 34° is unknown.*

$80$

> *The angle between the vertical line and the line **QR** will be the result of subtracting the bearing of **R** from **Q **from 180 because angles along a straight line add up to 180*<sup>*o*</sup>*.*

$180-155=25$

parts.solutionMd:

![4-11-edexcel-gcse-hq5](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/051-4-11-edexcel-gcse-hq5.png)

> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **C**. Substitute Area = 100, **a** = **y**, **b** = 8.4 and **C** = 40 into the formula.*

$\begin{aligned}100 & = & \frac{1}{2} \times y \times 8 . 4 \times sin \left(40\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange to get **y** by itself by multiplying both sides by 2 and dividing both sides by 8.4sin(40). Type into your calculator.*

$\begin{aligned}y & = & \frac{100 \times 2}{8 . 4 \times sin \left(40\right)} \\ & = & 37 . 041043 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *You now know the lengths of two sides and the angle between them and you want to find the length of the third side. Therefore you need to use the cosine rule.*

> *The formula for the cosine rule is *$a^{2}=b^{2}+c^{2}-2bc\mathrm{cos}A$*, where **b** and **c** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **A** and **a** is the length of the side opposite **A**. Substitute **a** = **x**, **b** = 8.4, **c** = 37.041043... (using the answer button) and **A** = 40 into the formula.*

$x^{2} = 8 . 4^{2} + 37 . 041043 . . .^{2} - 2 \left(8 . 4\right) \left(37 . 041043 . . .\right) cos \left(40\right)$

**[1]**

> *Type the expression into your calculator altogether as one line. If you do it separately you need to remember the order of operations (multiplication before addition).*

$x^{2}=965.897466...$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \sqrt{965 . 897466 . . .} \\ & = & 31 . 078891 . . .\end{aligned}$

$AB=31.1m(3\mathrm{sf})$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
In triangle $RPQ$,

Assuming that angle $PQR$is an acute angle, calculate the area of triangle $RPQ$.

parts.solutionMd:
> *Sketch the diagram and label the relevant sides and angles.*

![4-11-edexcel-gcse-hq6a](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/055-4-11-edexcel-gcse-hq6a.png)

> *To find the area of a triangle formula you need to know the lengths of two sides and the angle between them. We currently do not know angle **RPQ** so work out what you can.*

> *You know the length of one side and the angle opposite it. You also know the length of another side so you can use the sine rule to find the angle opposite it.*

> *The formula for the sine rule is *$\frac{\mathrm{sin}A}{a}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}B}{b}$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that are opposite the angles **A **and **B **respectively. *
*Substitute **a** = **8.7**, **b** = 5.2, **A** = **y** and **B** = 32 into the formula.*

$\frac{sin \left(y\right)}{8 . 7} = \frac{sin \left(32\right)}{5 . 2}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 8.7 and then find the angle by using the inverse sin function.*

$\begin{aligned}sin \left(y\right) & = & \frac{sin \left(32\right)}{5 . 2} \times 8 . 7 \\ y & = & sin^{- 1} \left(\frac{sin \left(32\right)}{5 . 2} \times 8 . 7\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Type into your calculator.*

$\begin{aligned}y & = & 62 . 448531 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *You can find the third angle by spotting that the three interior angles of the triangle should add up to 180°. Use the answer button on your calculator.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & 180 - 32 - 62 . 448531 . . . \\ & = & 85 . 551468 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *You now have enough information to find the area.*

> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **C**. Substitute **a** = 8.7, **b** = 5.2 and **C** = 85.551468... (using the answer button) into the formula.*

$\begin{aligned}Area & = & \frac{1}{2} \times 8 . 7 \times 5 . 2 \times sin \left(85 . 551468 . . .\right) \\ & = & 22 . 551855 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Round to 3 significant figures. Remember to include square units for the area.*

$\mathrm{Area}=22.6\mathrm{cm}^{2}(3\mathrm{sf})$** [1]**

> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **C**. Substitute Area = **A**, **a** = **x**, **b** = 2**x** and **C** = 30 into the formula.*

$\begin{aligned}A & = & \frac{1}{2} \times x \times 2 x \times sin \left(30\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Use the your calculator to find that *$sin \left(30\right) = \frac{1}{2}$*.*

$\begin{aligned}A & = & \frac{1}{2} \times x \times 2 x \times \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}A & = & \frac{1}{\cancel{2}} \times x \times \cancel{2} x \times \frac{1}{2} \\ A & = & \frac{x^{2}}{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 2.*

$\begin{aligned}x^{2} & = & 2 A\end{aligned}$

> *Take the positive square root of both sides.*

$x=\sqrt{2A}$ **[1]**

AB = 3km, AD = 5km, CD = 12km and angle BAC = 30°.

The land is sold for £10 million per square kilometre.

Calculate the total cost of the land.

£ .............................................. million
parts.solutionMd:
> *Calculate the area, **A**, of the triangle ADC using the area of a triangle formula, *$A=\frac{1}{2}\timesbase\timesheight$*.*

$\begin{aligned}A_{A D C} & = & \frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 5\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}A_{A D C} & = & 30\end{aligned}$

> *Calculate the length AC using Pythagoras' theorem, *$c^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}$*, on triangle ACD, where *$a$* and *$b$* are the lengths of the two shorter sides and *$c$* is the length of the hypotenuse.*

$\begin{aligned}AC^{2} & = & 5^{2} + 12^{2}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}AC & = & \sqrt{5^{2} + 12^{2}} \\ AC & = & \sqrt{25 + 144} \\ AC & = & \sqrt{169}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

$\begin{aligned}AC & = & 13\end{aligned}$

> *You can now find the area of triangle ABC, **A**, using the formula for the area of a triangle, *$A=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where *$a$* and *$b$* are two sides of the triangle and *$C$* is the angle in between them.*

$A_{ABC}=\frac{1}{2}\times3\times13\times\mathrm{sin}30$

**[1]**

> *Substitute the exact value *$\mathrm{sin}30=\frac{1}{2}$* into the equation.*

$A_{ABC}=\frac{1}{2}\times3\times13\times\frac{1}{2}$

**[1]**

> *Solve.*

$A_{ABC}=\frac{39}{4}=9.75$

> *Add the areas of both triangles together to find the total area of the land.*

$30+9.75=39.75$

**[1]**

> *Work out the total cost of the land by multiplying the total area by the cost per square kilometre.*

$10\times39.75$

`bold £ bold 397 bold. bold 5 bold space bold million`* ***[1]**

Calculate the distance of *B* from *A*.
Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solutionMd:
> **[exam-tip]**
> Whenever a visual problem has been described in words, first use the information provided to make a sketch of the situation. Label any angles or distances that have been given.

> *Draw a sketch of the described problem as shown below, ensuring that bearings are labelled clockwise from North*

![Triangle ABC with angles 105° at A and 230° at B. AC is 180 km, BC is 95 km. Northerly arrows N1 and N2 indicate direction.](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/001-triangle-abc-with-angles-105-at-a-and-230-at-b-a.png)

**[M1]**

> *Calculate angle **ABN*<sub>*2*</sub>* using the co-interior angles add up to 180*<sup>*o*</sup>* angle rule*

$180^{o}-105^{o}=75^{o}$

> *Calculate angle **ABC** using the angles at a point add up to 360*<sup>*o*</sup>* angle rule*

$360^{o}-230^{o}-75^{o}=55^{o}$

**[M1]**

> *Calculate angle **CAB**, using the sine rule, *$\frac{\mathrm{sin}A}{a}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}B}{b}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}C}{c}$*, substituting values in for angle **ABC **and side lengths **BC** and **AC*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{sin A}{a} & = & \frac{sin B}{b} \\ \frac{sin A}{95} & = & \frac{sin 55}{180} \\ sin A & = & \frac{sin 55}{180} \times 95 \\ A & = & sin^{- 1} \left(\frac{sin 55}{180} \times 95\right) \\ A & = & 25 . 615 . . . \left(angle C A B\right)\end{aligned}$

**[M1]**

> *Calculate angle **ACB** using the angles in a triangle add up to 180*<sup>*o *</sup>*angle rule*

$180-55-25.615...=99.385...$

> *Calculate the side length **AB **using the sine rule, *$\frac{a}{\mathrm{sin}A}=\frac{b}{\mathrm{sin}B}=\frac{c}{\mathrm{sin}C}$*, substituting in values for angles **ABC **and **ACB** and side length **AC*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{b}{sin B} & = & \frac{c}{sin C} \\ \frac{180}{sin 55} & = & \frac{x}{sin 99 . 385 . . .} \\ \frac{180}{sin 55} \times sin 99 . 385 & = & x \\ 216 . 798 . . . & = & x \end{aligned}$

**[M1]**

> *Round length of AB to 3 significant figures as stated in the question*

**Final answer:** **AB=217 km**

**[A1]**

> 
> **M1**: For substituting the values provided in the question the correctly calculated angle *ABC*=55<sup>o</sup> into the sine rule to calculate angle CAB.
> 
> **M1**: For showing a full and correct method for calculating the angle CAB. This mark is only awarded if a previous M1 mark is awarded.
> 
> **M1**: For showing a full and correct method using the sine or cosine rule to calculate the length AB. This mark is only awarded if a previous M1 mark is awarded and can be gained if you have used an incorrectly calculated value of angle *CAB*.

- *So, using triangle ABC, start by calculating the angle BAC (or BCA)*
- *Then you'll be able to find the length BD using SOHCAHTOA*

$a^{2}=b^{2}+c^{2}-2bc\mathrm{cos}A\,11^{2}=16^{2}+9^{2}-2\times16\times9\times\mathrm{cos}A$

parts.problemMd:
![q1-vhard-4-11-sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangge-edexcel-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/018-q1-vhard-4-11-sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-trian.png)

The area of triangle $ABC$ is $6\sqrt{2}$m<sup>2</sup>.

Calculate the value of $x$. 
Give your answer correct to $3$significant figures.
parts.solutionMd:
> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **C**. *
*Substitute Area = *$6\sqrt{2}$*, **a** = *$\left(x + 3\right)$*, **b** = *$\left(2 x - 1\right)$* and **C** = 45 into the formula.*

$\begin{aligned}6 \sqrt{2} & = & \frac{1}{2} \times \left(x + 3\right) \times \left(2 x - 1\right) \times sin \left(45\right)\end{aligned}$

**Correct expression on the right hand side**** [1] **
**Forming a correct equation ****[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 2 and divide both sides by sin(45).*

$\begin{aligned}\frac{2 \times 6 \sqrt{2}}{sin \left(45\right)} & = & \left(x + 3\right) \left(2 x - 1\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Type *$\begin{aligned} & & \frac{2 \times 6 \sqrt{2}}{sin \left(45\right)}\end{aligned}$* into your calculator to simplify that term.*

$\begin{aligned}24 & = & \left(x + 3\right) \left(2 x - 1\right)\end{aligned}$

> *Expand the brackets then simplify.*

$2x^{2}-x+6x-3=24\,2x^{2}+5x-3=24$

**[1]**

> *Subtract 24 from both sides to make the quadratic equal 0.*

$2x^{2}+5x-27=0$

> *As the question asks for 3 significant figures, this suggests that the quadratic does not factorise. Solve by using the quadratic formula, *$x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{b^{2}-4ac}}{2a}$*. Substitute **a** = 2, **b** = 5 and **c =** -27 into the formula.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{- 5 \pm \sqrt{5^{2} - 4 \left(2\right) \left(- 27\right)}}{2 \left(2\right)}\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify using your calculator.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{- 5 + \sqrt{241}}{4} = 2 . 631043 . . . \\ & & or \\ x & = & \frac{- 5 - \sqrt{241}}{4} = - 5 . 131043 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *As **x** + 3 is a length then it can not be negative, so **x** > -3. Therefore reject **x** = -5.131043... *
*Round the other solution to 3 significant figures.*

$x=2.63(3sf)$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
$ABC$and $ADC$are triangles.

![q2-vhard-4-11-sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangge-edexcel-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/025-q2-vhard-4-11-sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-trian.png)

The area of triangle $ADC$is 56 m<sup>2</sup>

Work out the length of $AB.$ 
Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.solutionMd:
> *First use the area to form an equation using triangle **ADC**.*

![4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq2-1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/026-4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq2-1.png)

> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **C**. *
*Substitute Area = 56, **a** = **z**, **b** = 11 and **C** = 105 into the formula.*

$\begin{aligned}56 & = & \frac{1}{2} \times z \times 11 \times sin \left(105\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Rearrange to get **z** by itself by multiplying both sides by 2 and dividing both sides by 11sin(105). Type into your calculator.*

$\begin{aligned}z & = & \frac{56 \times 2}{11 \times sin \left(105\right)} \\ & = & 10 . 540993 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *You now know the lengths of two sides and the angle between them and you want to find the length of the third side. Therefore you need to use the cosine rule.*

> *The formula for the cosine rule is *$a^{2}=b^{2}+c^{2}-2bc\mathrm{cos}A$*, where **b** and **c** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **A** and **a** is the length of the side opposite **A**. Substitute **a** = **y**, **b** = 11, **c** = 10.540993... (using the answer button) and **A** = 105 into the formula.*

$y^{2} = 11^{2} + 10 . 540993 . . .^{2} - 2 \left(11\right) \left(10 . 540993 . . .\right) cos \left(105\right)$

**[1]**

> *Type the expression into your calculator altogether as one line. If you do it separately you need to remember the order of operations (multiplication before addition).*

$y^{2}=292.133170...$

> *Take the positive square root of both sides.*

$\begin{aligned}y & = & \sqrt{292 . 133170 . . .} \\ & = & 17 . 091903 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Now use triangle **ABC**. You know the length of a side and the angle opposite it. You also know another angle so you can use the sine rule to find the length of the side opposite it.*

![4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq2-2](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/027-4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq2-2.png)

> *The formula for the sine rule is *$\frac{a}{\mathrm{sin}A}=\frac{b}{\mathrm{sin}B}$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that are opposite the angles **A **and **B **respectively. *
*Substitute **a** = **x**, **b** = 17.091903... (using the answer button), **A** = 48 and **B** = 118 into the formula.*

$\frac{x}{sin \left(48\right)} = \frac{17 . 091903 . . .}{sin \left(118\right)}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by sin(48) and type into your calculator.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & \frac{17 . 091903 . . .}{sin \left(118\right)} \times sin \left(48\right) \\ & = & 14 . 385632 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Round to 1 decimal place. Remember to include units for the length.*

$AB=14.4m(1\mathrm{dp})$* ***[1]**

parts.problemMd:
$ABCD$is a parallelogram.

 $DC$ = 11 cm

parts.solutionMd:
> *The parallelogram is split into two identical triangles. To use the formula for the area of a triangle you need two sides and the angle between them. You do not currently have this so use triangle **ACD** to help find the required angle.*

![4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/020-4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq3.png)

> *You know the length of one side and the angle opposite it. You also know the length of another side so you can use the sine rule to find the angle opposite it.*

> *The formula for the sine rule is *$\frac{\mathrm{sin}A}{a}=\frac{\mathrm{sin}B}{b}$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that are opposite the angles **A **and **B **respectively. *
*Substitute **a** = **9**, **b** = 11, **A** = **y** and **B** = 100 into the formula.*

$\frac{sin \left(y\right)}{9} = \frac{sin \left(100\right)}{11}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply both sides by 9 and then find the angle by using the inverse sin function.*

$\begin{aligned}sin \left(y\right) & = & \frac{sin \left(100\right)}{11} \times 9 \\ y & = & sin^{- 1} \left(\frac{sin \left(100\right)}{11} \times 9\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Type into your calculator.*

$\begin{aligned}y & = & 53 . 682923 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *You can find the third angle by spotting that the three interior angles of the triangle should add up to 180°. Use the answer button on your calculator.*

$\begin{aligned}x & = & 180 - 100 - 53 . 682923 . . . \\ & = & 26 . 317076 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *You now have enough information to find the area of one of the triangles.*

> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **C**. Substitute **a** = 9, **b** = 11 and **C** = 26.317076... (using the answer button) into the formula.*

$\begin{aligned}Area & = & \frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 11 \times sin \left(26 . 317076 . . .\right) \\ & = & 21 . 945249 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Multiply by 2 to find the area of the parallelogram.*

$\begin{aligned}2 \times 21 . 945249 . . . & = & 43 . 890498 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Round to 3 significant figures. Remember to include square units for the area.*

$\mathrm{Area}=43.9\mathrm{cm}^{2}(3\mathrm{sf})$** [1]**

parts.solutionMd:
> *First use the area to form an equation.*

![4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/010-4-11-edexcel-gcse-vhq4.png)

> *The formula for the area of a triangle is *$\mathrm{Area}=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **C**. *
*Substitute Area = 18, **a** = 8, **b** = 7 and **C** = **z** into the formula.*

$\begin{aligned}18 & = & \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 7 \times sin \left(z\right)\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *Simplify the equation. Then rearrange to find the value of **z**.*

$\begin{aligned}28 sin \left(z\right) & = & 18 \\ sin \left(z\right) & = & \frac{18}{28} \\ z & = & sin^{- 1} \left(\frac{18}{28}\right) \\ z & = & 40 . 005200 . . .\end{aligned}$

**[1]**

> *You now know the lengths of two sides and the angle between them so you can find the length of the third side using the cosine rule.*

> *The formula for the cosine rule is *$a^{2}=b^{2}+c^{2}-2bc\mathrm{cos}A$*, where **b** and **c** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **A** and **a** is the length of the side opposite **A**. Substitute **a** = **y**, **b** = 8, **c** = 8 and **A** = 40.005200... (using the answer button) into the formula.*

$y^{2} = 8^{2} + 7^{2} - 2 \left(8\right) \left(8\right) cos \left(40 . 005200 . . .\right)$

**[1]**

> *Type the expression into your calculator altogether as one line. If you do it separately you need to remember the order of operations (multiplication before addition).*

$y^{2}=27.209557...$

**[1]**

> *Take the positive square root of both sides.*

> *The formula for the sine rule is *$\frac{a}{\mathrm{sin}A}=\frac{b}{\mathrm{sin}B}$*, where **a** and **b** are the lengths of the two sides that are opposite the angles **A **and **B **respectively. Substitute **a** = **AD**, **b** = 10, **A** = 112.5 and **B** = 22.5 into the formula.*

$\frac{A D}{sin \left(112 . 5\right)} = \frac{10}{sin \left(22 . 5\right)}$

![q25-paper2h-june2017-aqa-gcse-maths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SyllabAI/syllabai-resources/main/SME-ExamQuestion/igcse-maths-a-18-higher/4-geometry-and-trigonometry/sine-cosine-rule-and-area-of-triangles/assets/011-q25-paper2h-june2017-aqa-gcse-maths.png)

Show that the area of the logo is 510 cm<sup>2</sup> to 2 significant figures.
parts.solutionMd:
> *The area of the logo is the area of the two triangles added to the area of the sector.*

> *Find the area of the triangles using the area of a triangle formula, *$A=\frac{1}{2}ab\mathrm{sin}C$*, where *$a$* and *$b$* are the two known sides and *$C$* is the included angle. The triangles are congruent, which means identical, so the calculation is the same for both of them.*

$Area_{triangle} = \frac{1}{2} \times \left(15\right) \times \left(26\right) \times sin \left(38\right) = 195 sin 38$

**[1]**

> *It is best to leave working as exact values where possible as you work through the problem so leaving it in terms of sin here will make it easier to work with later. *

> *To find the area of the sector, you will first need to find its radius. You know the lengths of two sides and the angle between them of the triangle and the radius of the sector is the side opposite the angle, so you can use the cosine rule, *$a^{2}=b^{2}+c^{2}-2bc\mathrm{cos}A$*, where **b** and **c** are the lengths of the two sides that form angle **A** and **a** is the length of the side opposite **A**.*

$r ^{2} = 26 ^{2} + 15 ^{2} - 2 ( 26 ) ( 15 ) cos ( 38 )$
$r = \sqrt{26 ^{2} + 15 ^{2} - 2 ( 26 ) ( 15 ) \text{cos} ( 38 ) }$

**[1]**

> *Type the expression into your calculator altogether as one line to get a value for **r.*

$\begin{aligned}r & = & 16 . 921926 . . .\end{aligned}$

> *Find the area of the sector** **using the formula for area of a sector *$=\frac{θ}{360^{\circ}}\timesπr^{2}$*, the angle for the sector is *$θ=108$* and use the unrounded value found for **r.** *

$Area_{s e c t o r} = \frac{108}{360} \times \pi \times \left(16 . 921926\right)^{2} = 269 . 880036 . . .$

**Correct fraction**** [1] **
**Correct method to find area**** [1]**

> *Find the area of the logo by adding 2 lots of the area of the triangle to the area of the sector**.*

*Area logo = *$2 \left(195 sin 38\right) + 269 . 880036 . . .$

**Final answer:** **Area = **$509.988...=510\mathrm{cm}^{2}(2s.f.)$** ****[1]**
